News.title: Missing fisherman, 31, rescued ALIVE after spending 15 days trapped 300ft down pitch-black underwater cave
News.content:
A FISHERMAN has been rescued after a harrowing 15-days trapped 300ft down a water-filled sinkhole.

Erasto Crisanto Valdez ,31, vanished while fishing with his father in a cenote in San Francisco La Paz, Mexico, on July 23.



After over two weeks missing, rescuers presumed the man as dead and were “prepared to find his body”.

By some miracle he was found alive – reportedly trapped in a cave with an air pocket more than 328ft below the surface.



He was discovered on Thursday by a international team of explorers from Mexico, Germany, the US and the Dominican Republic after facing weeks of cold and humidity in the dark cave.

Mexican explorer Carlos Jiménez described the discovery as a miracle saying “god had other plans” for the lucky man.

In an interview with NMás, Erasto said: “Thank you god for giving me another opportunity at life and letting me see my kids and family again.

“It was a miracle – an unbelievable miracle”



Following his initial disappearance, a search operation began immediately, but searches in the water yielded no results.

Six days into the desperate search rescuers discovered found the harpoon Erasto.

The depth of the cenote and the difficult conditions at the site made it challenging to locate Erasto.



A cenote is a deep natural well or sinkhole formed by the collapse of surface limestone, exposing groundwater beneath.

Erasto was then brought to the surface on a stretcher.

He was found to be suffering from severe dehydration and malnutrition after spending more than two weeks without access to food,

He was rushed to hospital for treatment in his hometown of Uxpanapa.

It comes as five people were saved from a flooded cave in Laos after they became trapped.



Thai rescuers successfully pulled five of the seven villagers from the tiny after torrential rain triggered landslides that sealed the entrance in May.

The villagers ventured into the remote cave in Xaysomboun province in May reportedly hunting for wildlife and searching for gold.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sadly two men were never found as the active search was called off when rescue teams deemed it too dangerous.

The rescue was led by the same team who saved the Thai football team who became trapped in the Tham Luang Nang Non cave system in 2018.

News.title: Iran military chief threatens to ‘break Trump’s legs’ after US leader vowed to make Strait of Hormuz American territory
News.content:
ONE of Iran’s top military chiefs has threatened to break Donald Trump’s legs after the US President vowed to make the Strait of Hormuz American territory.

Responding to Trump’s incendiary remarks, Major General Amir Hatami said joking about such a move was a “major mistake” because Iran had defenders who would “break your legs”.



He also claimed US forces had been “effectively driven out” of the region and would no longer be permitted to enter the fiercely contested Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian officials had previously told the White House to “accept the reality of defeat” after Tehran declared it would not resume talks with Washington.



The comments came after Trump confidently declared that the crucial gateway to the Gulf would one day become “a territory of the United States”.

Trump said: “After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated – pretty soon, I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.”

“Essentially, that’s what it is. We have the blockade.

“No ships get through unless we want them to.”



Before the US launched strikes on Iran earlier this year, the Strait of Hormuz was one of the world’s most crucial maritime routes for oil tankers.

But since the outbreak of war, passage through the strait has become increasingly difficult and, at times, has been completely halted.

The disruption has sent shockwaves through global markets, with oil prices soaring amid fears over supplies.

With no imminent peace deal in sight, Hatami also announced a $30,000 bounty for any US service member who is captured or killed.

“Given the large volume of requests to participate in the financial jihad, a plan was prepared according to which, for every person who kills or captures and hands over an American aggressor force, the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, with the support of the loved ones participating in the financial jihad and under its own guarantee, will receive a gift equivalent to $30,000 or 5 billion Tomans,” Hatami said.



“The weapon of any person who succeeds in killing an American aggressor will be purchased at double the price and will receive a new weapon.

“The individual’s weapon will also be kept in a planned museum.”

The Iranian military chief also issued a stark warning to US forces and bases across the Middle East.



“Everyone should know that in no way can the American bases return to their previous status, and Iran will never allow centers to be established in our neighborhood that aim to threaten Islamic Iran,” he said.

“The only way is for the Americans to leave the region. They have been effectively expelled and are no longer permitted to enter the Persian Gulf, the Sea of Oman, and the Strait of Hormuz.

“We have won on this path and are consolidating our victory.”

The extraordinary threats come as Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and envoy, held rare talks with Hamas in a bid to revive the stalled Gaza peace process.

Kushner met with a senior Hamas leader on Sunday as part of a renewed diplomatic push to advance the US-backed ceasefire plan.



He is due to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday for talks aimed at salvaging a 15-point roadmap backed by Washington.

The plan requires Hamas to disarm in Gaza while Israel withdraws its forces from the war-torn territory.

At stake is the future of around two million people in Gaza and the reconstruction of the densely populated enclave, which remains largely under Israeli military control more than 10 months after the ceasefire halted major fighting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A meeting last year between Kushner, fellow US envoy Steve Witkoff and Hamas leaders in Egypt helped secure the original ceasefire.

But the agreement has since stalled over the key issue of Hamas disarmament.

News.title: Cops launch fresh appeal four years after murder of man, 22, as balaclava-clad gang still terrorising city
News.content:
MURDER RIDDLE Cops launch fresh appeal four years after murder of man, 22, as balaclava-clad gang still terrorising city

COPS have launched a fresh appeal for information four years on from the murder of a man as a balaclava-clad gang continue to terrorise the city.

Sam Rimmer, 22, was fatally shot in August 2022 at Lavrock Bank, Liverpool with ten people previously arrested – but no one has been charged.



It’s the four-year anniversary of when Sam was hit by one of eight bullets fired from an e-bike rider using a Czech-made military grade firearm.

He had been hanging out with friends when he was tragically caught in the crossfire of gangs battling to dominate the firearms and drugs trade.



Detectives believe the four murder suspects are part of a gang that had previously spent hours circling the area on two bikes to “hunt” for targets.

Wearing black masks, they used a type of horn or engine noise to bait the rival group, before firing towards Sam and his friends – some of who were also hit.



The murder weapon has been identified as a Skorpion sub-machine gun – capable of firing multiple shots in a fraction of a second.

But it has never been recovered and cops are unable to hand out justice unless crucial eye witnesses come forward.



Det Ch Insp Steve McGrath told the BBC: “I would still ask [anyone] to come forward and the reason for that really is I can assure you that the people who are involved in Sam’s murder directly – those four individuals on the bike – are still involved in serious criminality in and around the Dingle area as well.”

Five days after Sam’s death, council worker Ashley Dale, 28, was found dead of a gunshot wound in a back garden in the city’s Old Swan area.

And, Olivia Pratt-Korbel, nine, was also shot dead in her own home after Thomas Cashman burst into the property chasing a local criminal.

The deaths of these innocent people are as a result of a new generation of teen gangs in Merseyside using violence to replace the ‘old mafia’, according to a BBC Panorama investigation.

Speaking on the anniversary of Sam’s death, McGrath, added: “Today marks four years since Sam was murdered and I can only imagine how difficult this occasion must be for his family and friends.



“I want to reassure them, and the wider community in Dingle, that we are still just as determined to find the people responsible as we were four years ago.

“As part of our investigation we have made a number of arrests and received a lot of information from the public. We just need the final piece of the puzzle.

“I’d like to take this opportunity to appeal to anyone who holds any information whatsoever to get in touch. It’s not too late.

“We are certain that someone out there knows who is responsible and could end the family’s agonising wait for answers.

“If anyone out there is keeping information to themselves, I ask you to consider what Sam’s family are going through.



“If you haven’t already, it is now time to come forward with that information.”

Pamela Tompsett, North West Regional Manager at the charity Crimestoppers said: “It’s now four years on from Sam’s tragic murder, his family and friends are still waiting for answers and justice.

“It is possible that someone knows who is responsible or holds information that could help investigators but has not yet felt able to speak directly to the police.

“Crimestoppers is completely independent of the police, and anyone contacting us remains 100 per cent anonymous.

“We have no caller ID, we do not trace IP addresses, and we never ask for personal details.



“The reward of up to £20,000 is available for information we exclusively receive that leads to the conviction of those responsible for Sam’s murder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If you know something, however small it may seem, please tell us anonymously. Your information could be the missing piece that helps brings answers for Sam’s family and justice for those responsible.”

Anyone with information should contact Merseyside Police social media desk using X or Facebook @MerPolCC. or by calling 101.

News.title: Reform vows to BAN foreign nationals from claiming benefits in £50bn welfare shake-up
News.content:
FOREIGN nationals will be stopped from claiming benefits if Reform UK come to power.

Nigel Farage’s party is planning a major shake-up of the “plain immoral” welfare system in a bid to save £50billion a year.



But it would mean renegotiating the Brexit deal with Brussels as the ban would also include EU citizens with settled status.

And that could mean British expats living in member states losing their equivalent rights.



In a speech today, Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick will say that unless savings are made to the welfare bill — set to hit £407billion by 2030 — it will “bankrupt Britain and send taxes higher”.

He will add: “Forcing British workers to pay for the benefits of foreigners is not just economically illiterate but plain immoral. British taxpayers cannot afford to subsidise everyone on the planet, especially those who have not paid in. The public have been crying out for this change for decades.”



Reform says only a limited number of exemptions will apply, such as those claiming the War Widows Pension and Armed Forces compensation.

The move would help boost Treasury coffers by £21billion by the fifth year in operation.

The party previously outlined its plans to stop foreign nationals claiming Universal Credit.

But its new proposals extend to housing benefit, pension credit, child benefit, jobseekers’ allowance, disability benefits and free childcare.



Mr Jenrick also put forward plans to save £22billion from the welfare bill by targeting sickness and disability benefits.

Labour has blasted Reform’s plan, saying it would “plunge the UK back into years of Brexit negotiations”.

A spokesman added it will “strip support from potentially millions of people who have lawfully lived, worked and paid taxes in Britain for years, and in many cases decades”.

News.title: Grieving family of student killed by drunk hit-&-run driver write open letter begging PM to block killer’s early release
News.content:
THE parents of a law student killed by a drunk hit-and-run driver have written a letter urging the PM to block the killer’s early release.

Abigail Eggleston, 22, was hit last October in Durham by Liam Bowes, 37.



He got 12 years in March, which may now get cut. ­

Justice Secretary Alex Norris is to present a plan to Parliament next month for changes to the early-release scheme.



Here is the letter:

Dear Prime Minister,



Our daughter Abigail Eggleston who was ­studying law at Durham was killed in a fatal hit and run incident last year whilst on a night out.

The defendant drove through a red light at speed whilst heavily ­intoxicated, and left my daughter for dead.

He next set fire to the car, went into hiding at a friend’s house and sent a message to his mate stating he was starving and arranged ordering a pizza.

We were already absolutely devastated at the length of his sentence (just 12 years of which he will only spend eight in prison).



His crime, in our opinions, is basically murder and it is within our intentions to start a campaign against the current leniency.

Our daughter’s killer was only sentenced in March of this year and we are still dealing with our grief, trauma and total disapproval and disappointment at the short sentence he was given.

However, as if that were not already bad enough, we have been contacted by the Probation Officer, informing us in writing that there is the potential he may be given a reduced sentence to ease overcrowding in prisons.

In the meantime, we are left with this uncertainty until the end of August, which is basically torture and immoral.

This news has hit us like a sledgehammer, it is basically insult to injury. [Abigail’s dad] Andy, who is severely disabled by MS, has taken this news very badly and has indicated it is the final straw for him and that he intends to end his misery by going to Dignitas.



This is obviously extra upsetting and distressing for myself and other daughter.

It disgusts us that the Government’s solution to an increasing problem is to reward the criminals by ­presenting them with early release, leaving the victim’s families/loved ones and friends to deal with further trauma and distress.

We are urging the Government to urgently change their minds.

From Mandy and Andy Eggleston, parents of Abigail

In response to the letter, a Ministry of Justice spokesman said: “We have always stated we wanted to go further, and we are fast-tracking a plan to keep more of the most dangerous offenders behind bars.

“That’s on top of murderers and those serving sentences for rape, serious child sexual abuse and grooming offences who are already blocked from any changes.



“We share the public’s anger that these options are even being considered, after we inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are fixing this by building 14,000 new prison places, expanding electronic tagging on an unprecedented scale, and investing in probation services at record levels.

“We are also exploring how we can go further, including faster deportation of foreign criminals, better use of the women’s estate and reviewing the unjust IPP sentences.”

News.title: Vickrum Digwa gets cosy prison calls with mum while Henry Nowak’s family are denied justice
News.content:
No justice

HOW Henry Nowak’s grieving mother Lucy would love a video call with her son.

To see his smiling face. To hear the latest on his finance studies.



But she can’t, ever again, since the 18-year-old’s life was brutally taken by murderer Vickrum Digwa.

How sickening, then, that Digwa — rightly serving a life sentence — will be allowed cosy inter-prison video calls to his own mum Kiran Kaur after she was herself jailed for being complicit in the killing by hiding the murder weapon.



Her devious actions, before police arrived on the scene, helped Digwa’s foul pretence that he was the victim and contributed to officers wrongly arresting fatally-stabbed and totally innocent Henry, leaving him “dying terrified, alone and disbelieved”.

It’s scant comfort to Henry’s family that Kaur is actually in jail, but even that could end pretty soon despite her getting a three-year sentence last month.

As the Government prepares for the early release of thousands of prisoners — including wife-beaters, hit-and-run drivers and the remorseless killers of PC Andrew Harper — and the police and public brace for a surge in cases of theft and violence as a result, the shameful state of the justice system is glaring.

It’s not just soft justice. It’s no justice.

Cross divides

CONTROLLED migration has benefitted the UK hugely over the years, not least in our NHS and social care.

And foreign workers who followed the rules to come here — and grafted hard to make this country their home — are among those outraged by the number of uncontrolled economic migrants drawn across the Channel by a ludicrously over-generous welfare system.



Tens of thousands of mostly fighting-age young men coming here unhindered by border controls is an affront to law-abiding UK citizens from all walks of life — not just the wealthier areas the PM thinks should house more of them.

So is the no-questions-asked handout of billions in welfare every year, and the vast sums squandered to fraud and lazy governance.

As long as Andy Burnham’s Government fails to stop the Channel boats AND fails to tackle the unsustainable welfare bill, those who seek to sow division are more likely to succeed.

Tapped up

CONSUMERS in the grip of a hosepipe ban are set to be soaked by the companies responsible for polluting our rivers and losing so much of our water to leaking pipes.

Government approval of so-called “surge pricing” will hasten the arrival of water meters for all and see water costs rocket in times of drought.



As campaigner Feargal Sharkey says, the firms will be penalising Brits, and reward-ing themselves, for their own failures.

News.title: Fury as Henry Nowak’s evil killer is allowed prison-to-prison video chats with jailbird mum who hid murder weapon
News.content:
HENRY Nowak’s killer is to be allowed ­prison-to-prison video calls with his mother, sparking fury.

Kiran Kaur is in jail for hiding murderer ­Vickrum Digwa’s knife in Southampton.



A source said: “Henry’s family won’t get to see him again. It’s beyond a joke.”

Letting killer Vickrum Digwa have video calls with his jailbird mum has infuriated prison staff — and is another blow for Henry Nowak’s family, sources said last night.



Digwa had an application approved for online video chats — called “Purple Visits” — with Kiran Kaur, 53, despite her hiding the knife her son used to kill student Henry.

The murderer, 23, held at HMP ­Frankland, Durham, is set to have one of the calls within weeks to Kaur, in Bronzefield Prison, Surrey.

A source said: “The fact Digwa will be allowed the video calls with his mum has angered people, including many of the staff at Frankland. They think it’s a ­disgrace that they have to go to the effort of arranging them.

“Poor Henry’s family won’t get to see him again so why should Digwa be allowed to speak to his mum via video-link? It is beyond a joke and we go too far to accommodate the needs of killers.”

Digwa is serving at least 21 years for 18-year-old Henry’s murder in Southampton last December.

Kaur got three years for hiding his ­eight-inch blade at home.



After the fatal attack, Digwa also lied to police that he had been the victim of racism.

Police bodycam footage later showed officers arresting Henry as he repeatedly said he was stabbed, telling them: “I can’t breathe.”

The sickening circumstances ­surrounding the murder has made the Purple Visit approval more appalling, our source said.



They went on: “Governors have to judge each application on its merits.

“But the idea of this happening is horrible given the nature of the crime — and the fact his mum got involved after the murder and hid the weapon. But now she has been convicted and sentenced there is no longer a danger of them discussing the crime and affecting her case.”

There was said to be little chance of the application getting turned down.

The source continued: “He’d be able to claim his human rights were breached and have all these lobby groups standing up for him.

“Digwa has been in touch with the Samaritans and the ­Independent Monitoring Board since he’s been in Frankland.



“And the IMB, who ­regularly visit the jail, will have told him he is within his rights to have these calls and might have helped him to apply.”

Digwa and his mother were convicted in May, with Kaur sentenced last month.

Henry’s family, including his sister Olivia and mum Lucy Ross, released a statement saying they were “incredibly disappointed” at the three-year term handed down at Southampton crown court.

But they promised to continue to fight for the “full truth”.



Reform MP Robert Jenrick said: “While Henry Nowak’s family and friends struggle to get over their loss and his ­terrible death, his despicable killer is enjoying perks in jail.

“He shouldn’t have any ­privileges — it’s a disgrace — and should not be allowed to speak to his mother who hid the murder weapon.”

Justice sources said Digwa had not yet had a call with his mum. When they do, the pair will be told they have to speak in English so they can be ­monitored.

Digwa’s family also speak Punjabi — with he and his brother Gurpreet recorded by police talking in the language in a van on the way to court.



The insider explained: “Digwa will be put in a room with a tablet or laptop linked to his mum on a device in her jail and staff will be outside the door at each prison.

“But it would also be monitored in the security room — and if they started to speak Punjabi or to ­discuss the murder the call would be cut off. Staff will have to warn him about that and it will be one of the conditions of the call.”

Sikh Digwa — described as “weapons-obsessed” at his murder trial — was held in Winchester Prison before being moved to HMP Frankland at the end of June.

He has since cowered in segregation, fearing he could be targeted on a wing like Soham killer Ian Huntley, who was fatally attacked at the jail in February.



REMOTE ‘PURPLE VISIT’ By MICHAEL HAMILTON A “PURPLE Visit” call is designed to replicate a typical prison interaction with loved ones, but on a videolink instead. They are mainly used for relatives on the outside — and less frequently between two inmates. Authorisation from governors is needed for calls between prisoners. They are sometimes used by families with more than one member behind bars in different jails in the UK. Inmates are taken to a room to have their calls — usually lasting around 45 minutes — with staff positioned outside. All calls can be monitored — with security teams particularly listening into those made by high-profile prisoners. The Purple Visits app is used by prisons and other establishments as it is deemed “ultra-secure”. Its website boasts of “military-grade encryption” that “keeps your family conversations completely safe and confidential”. The Ministry of Justice says Purple Visits are available on application and are considered on a “case-by-case basis”.

But he is now terrified after being moved on to a landing last week.

He has also been warned he is a target — especially from Polish gangsters said to want revenge due to Henry’s heritage.

Our source added: “Digwa is on a wing now and it’s fair to say he’s s****ing himself. He has been warned he is a target for many groups — but particularly Polish gangsters. Although Henry was English, they see him as one of their own because of his name and Polish heritage.

“They see it as a racist killing of a Polish lad and want revenge.

“But Digwa could have problems from anyone and there are some white supremacists in there, plus ex-military, who would hate him for what he’s done.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Prison Service said: “This prisoner is being managed within the prison estate in line with the severity of the heinous offences for which he was convicted.”

The Sun contacted representatives for the Nowak family.

News.title: Somali man, 22, charged with attempted murder after worker ‘stabbed’ at migrant hotel near Heathrow airport
News.content:
HOTEL HORROR Somali man, 22, charged with attempted murder after worker ‘stabbed’ at migrant hotel near Heathrow airport

A SOMALI man has been charged with attempted murder after a support staff worker was stabbed at a hotel reportedly used to house asylum seekers.

Abdifatah Yusuf Adani, 22, allegedly stabbed a man in his 30s at the Stanwell hotel in Surrey, near Heathrow airport, at 6.30pm yesterday.

Armed officers raced to the scene and the victim was rushed to hospital after suffering life-threatening injuries.

Thankfully, he is now in a “stable condition” and Adani remains in custody, with a heavy police presence still at the scene.





He will appear at Staines Magistrates’ Court on Monday morning at 10am.

Conservative MP Lincoln Jopp posted a video on Facebook today in which he said the victim of the stabbing was a staff worker.

He said he received a phone call on Saturday from the chief constable of Surrey Police informing him of the stabbing.

Mr Jopp, MP for Spelthorne, said “one of the support staff who work here was stabbed”, and that “one of the people who live here was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder”.

Police previously said they were not looking for anyone else in relation to the incident, and asked anyone with information to get in touch.

Detective Superintendent Kate Hyder said on Saturday: “We understand this incident has caused concern within the local community, and I encourage you to speak to local officers.”

A statement from the Met read: “Abdifatah Yusuf Adani, 22, has this evening been charged with one count of attempted murder following a report of a stabbing at the Stanwell Hotel in Stanwell at 6.30pm yesterday evening.

“Adani, a Somalian national, has been remanded in custody and will appear at Staines Magistrates Court tomorrow morning at 10am.



“The victim, a man in his 30s who is a staff worker at the hotel, is now in a stable condition and his injuries are no longer thought to be life threatening.

“There remains a heightened police presence in the area.”

News.title: Five teenagers dead and four injured after car drives on wrong side of motorway
News.content:
Five teenage boys have died and four people have been taken to hospital following a two-vehicle crash in County Kildare.

The collision occurred on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time on Sunday.

GardaÃ­ said the bodies of the five teenage boys, all occupants of one vehicle, have now been removed from the scene and taken to Naas General Hospital where post mortems will take place.

They said the vehicle had been travelling on the wrong side of the carriageway when a head on collision occurred with a second car.

The driver and front passenger, both female and aged in their 30s, of the second car have been removed from the scene to Tallaght University Hospital and both remain in critical condition.

A female rear seat passenger, aged in her 20s, was taken to St. Luke's General Hospital and is in a serious condition.

The third passenger, who is a child, has been removed to Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin and is in a serious condition.

The section of the M9 from Junction 3 to Junction 4 northbound and southbound remains closed with local diversions in place.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly described those injured in the crash as "family members" who were "travelling innocently" when they were struck by the car driving on the wrong side of the motorway.

He described it as a "horrific incident" and "irresponsible and dangerous driving".

"What makes this reckless behaviour even more appalling is that in some cases it is being done for social media likes regardless of the potentially devastating impact it might have on innocent people and themselves."

Kelly added that officers "do what they can to stop such vehicles while also taking into consideration all other road users".

"GardaÃ­ are put in a really challenging situation dealing with such incidents."

News.title: Emergency phone alert put domestic abuse victims at risk, campaigners say
News.content:
Most people received the blaring alert at 19:00 BST on Friday - and it came as a surprise given the government had not told people it was coming, as it has done for tests of the system.

The notification, which cautioned against the use of disposable barbecues, naked flames or fireworks, was the biggest use yet of the emergency alert system and Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged the public to take it "seriously".

A Cabinet Office press release, posted to their website at about 18:45 on Friday, was missed by many in the media, which meant there was little warning to the public.

This potentially jeopardised domestic abuse victims trying to hide secret phones they use to seek support and try to escape abusers, some campaigners have said.

Women's Aid, the national charity aiming to end domestic abuse, is calling for more forewarning of alerts wherever possible.

Veronica Oakeshott, the charity's head of external affairs, told BBC News: "Survivors of domestic abuse frequently turn to second phones to help them access lifesaving support or flee from abuse."

It is vital the devices stay hidden, she said, before adding: "We would urge the government to forewarn the public that alerts might be issued, when possible."

It has been reported that senior government figures were discussing whether or not to send the alert hours before, on Friday morning.

The alert came after a spate of wildfires including one that destroyed 19 homes in Stourbridge, West Midlands, on Thursday.

News.title: Murder inquiry after man bitten by dog dies
News.content:
A murder inquiry has begun after the death of a man who was bitten by a dog on a footpath in West Yorkshire.

The 55-year-old was injured in an altercation on a disused railway line off Blacker Lane in Calder Grove, Wakefield, at about 13:30 BST on Saturday. He was taken to hospital in a critical condition but died just after 19:00.

West Yorkshire Police has appealed for two people, one of whom is called Sophie, who stopped to help the injured man to come forward.

A force spokesperson said a 55-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder and of being the owner of a dog dangerously out of control in a public place, causing injury. He remains in custody.

Police said a German Shepherd dog believed to have been involved in the incident has been seized by officers.

Det Ch Insp Michael Cox said: "Sadly, a man has died and it is really important that we understand the circumstances of what has taken place.

"We know that two people, one named Sophie, stopped to assist the injured man and direct officers."

He added: "We would urge these two people to come forward to help us with our ongoing inquiries into this tragic incident.

"The initial altercation happened in an area used by walkers and we are urging anyone who has seen or heard any part of the exchange between these two men to please make contact."

News.title: Calls for public inquiry into Jason Arday 'witch hunt'
News.content:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski, and Labour MPs Bell Ribiero-Addy, Clive Lewis and Nadia Whittome are among the politicians to have signed the statement, alongside former England footballer Eni Aluko, National Education Union general secretary Daniel Kebede, and broadcaster Carol Vorderman.

It calls for an "immediate public inquiry into how to ensure a responsible press".

Arday, 41, was found dead at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday. He had resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education on 5 August after allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. He had denied the claims.

Liverpool John Moores University - which awarded Arday his PhD in 2015 - concluded that he had not plagiarised work.

The row first erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in the professor's work. Cofnas's post had been terminated amid a backlash to his view that under a true meritocracy black people would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment".

Lord Woolley told BBC Radio 4's Broadcasting House programme on Sunday he and a number of close friends had met Arday four days before he was found dead at a south London address.

He said Abbott and social activist Misan Harriman were among those who gathered to offer support as they had also experienced "horrible media attention".

He said Arday felt "hounded" and the relentless media coverage had been "a bloodsport".

"Diane said to him, she held his hand, and said we will help you get through this," he added.

"But on that day, we saw a man half his body weight and desperate beyond belief."

Lord Woolley said issues of plagiarism were constant in academia and that a number of individuals, who had been accused of plagiarism had not been subjected to the attention Arday had received.

"We have to ask this question, we have to talk about - which a lot of people don't want to talk about, is racism. You have to look at negatively differential treatment."

On 6 August Cambridge announced an independent investigation into Arday's appointment.

It is understood the university does not feel it right to decide on whether to proceed with its investigation.

But one of the academic's friends, Sir Simon Baron-Cohen, told Times Radio on Sunday it should go ahead to "see what we learn from it" because "this is the whole purpose of investigations".

A University of Cambridge spokesperson told the BBC that during his time at the university, Arday had received a range of support in relation to his physical and mental well-being, including counselling and support and advice.

"Our support continued in the face of intense public and media scrutiny and after his resignation," they added.

Cambridge celebrated Arday's appointment as a young black professor, one of a tiny and visible minority in academia. Only one per cent of professors in UK universities are black, making each appointment hugely significant.

More than Â£90,000 has now been raised for Arday's family, after Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, who is also among the signatories to the petition, launched a fundraiser.

A vigil organised by group Stand Up To Racism is set to take place on Monday evening in Trafalgar Square.

News.title: Changing pubs into homes to be made harder under new rules
News.content:
The Campaign for Real Ale has previously said that pubs are being "lost forever to conversion or demolition as developers look to cash in on the desirable locations and unique architecture of pubs and social clubs".

The British Beer and Pub Association and UKHospitality have also campaigned against pub closures, with both largely blaming tax rises and other costs.

Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, said: "The biggest issue facing hospitality businesses is costs like VAT and business rates pushing pubs out of business in the first place.

"Anything that makes it harder to take these important assets away from their communities has to be welcomed, but the government should focus on continuing its strong start on fixing the harm done to hospitality over the past two years."

In July, the Labour government said pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England will be given a 20% cut to business rates on top of rates relief announced in January.

The NPPF update being published Monday also includes default approval for homes being built around railway stations in England in an attempt to increase housebuilding numbers.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner said: "By unlocking thousands of homes around well-connected transport hubs, we're helping people live closer to work, school and the services they rely on, while backing local businesses and driving growth in our communities."

The update also means that some groups will no longer need to be consulted on housing development plans as part of the process of getting permission.

The Gardens Trust, a parks and gardens heritage and conversion charity, called the decision to remove its role as a statutory consultee "devastating".

It said it devalued parks and gardens and "makes them vulnerable to poorly informed development".

Under the changes, the Gardens Trust and Theatres Trust will still be notified of relevant applications and Sport England will continue to advise on significant cases.

Labour has set a target to build 1.5 million homes by 2029. According to official data, external, it has so far built 392,000 homes in England since coming into power in July 2024.

Shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said Labour is "failing abysmally" to meet their target because of taxes and red tape.

"To try to fix their own mess, Labour are planning a power grab, seizing control from local communities and forcing them to accept development in the wrong areas because Labour won't build in the right areas," he added.

News.title: Reform UK benefits ban for foreign nationals would include EU citizens
News.content:
It is the latest announcement ahead of a speech on Monday by Reform's shadow chancellor Robert Jenrick to formally unveil the party's welfare plans.

"Forcing British workers to pay for the benefits of foreigners is not just economically illiterate but plain immoral," Jenrick said in a statement.

"People are more than happy to support their neighbours in hard times, but the British taxpayer cannot afford to subsidise everyone on the planet, especially those who have not paid in."

This year the government expects, external to spend a total of Â£322bn on welfare in Great Britain, or 10.6% of GDP, just over half of which goes to pensioners.

Reform says it has spent six months drawing up a 50-page plan that it claims will save a total of Â£50bn a year.

On Saturday, the party said it would replace the disability payments system, Pip, if it entered Number 10 at the next election.

The latest proposals would ban foreign nationals from almost all welfare payments including housing benefit, pension credit, jobseeker's allowance, child benefit, free childcare and disability benefits.

Only a small number of exemptions would apply, including the war widows pension and Armed Forces compensation.

The party had previously pledged to ban foreign nationals from claiming Universal Credit.

News.title: Watch moment police arrest wanted man while he slept on roof
News.content:
A stand-off involving a wanted man was brought to an end when police arrested him while he slept on a roof.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said emergency services had responded to an incident at a property on Reservoir Street in Salford, spending two days at the scene.

Footage shows officers from the force's tactical unit gently resting a ladder against the roof of a back porch, with an officer then grabbing the man while he was sleeping.

A struggle ensues and the man is pulled down, with his trousers appearing to fall down, before he is arrested by officers in the garden of the property.

Two police officers suffered minor injuries during the incident on Saturday.

GMP said it was asked by another force to arrest the man who was wanted on recall to prison for other matters.

The force said a 37-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing public nuisance, criminal damage, public order offences, burglary and assaulting two police officers.

He remains in police custody.

Det Ch Insp Helen Bagnall said: "During two days of disruption to the local community, we worked continuously with our partners to bring this matter to a safe conclusion.

"This was an extensive use of vital policing resources and clearly demonstrates the dangers our officers face on a daily basis in order to protect the people of Greater Manchester."

She thanked the people of Salford for their "patience and understanding" while emergency services dealt with the incident, adding some properties had been damaged as a result of the man's actions.

She said the force would work with partners to ensure affected residents would be supported.

News.title: US women in politics spark conversation on motherhood
News.content:
Last summer, Representative Sara Jacobs would run up to her office to give herself injections of hormones before rushing back to Congress for a session with her fellow lawmakers.

The shots were for the second round of freezing her eggs, a medical procedure that can give women more time to have children.

"It was an empowering decision that gave me more agency," the 37-year-old said, adding that the process was challenging.

"Your body hurts. Your hormones are crazy. It's kind of like puberty and menopause at the same time."

Jacobs announced she was beginning the egg freezing process in 2021, at a time when she said few lawmakers were discussing the topic in the halls of Congress.

The process - which can cost more than $10,000 (Â£7,400) and is rarely covered by insurance - involves doctors harvesting eggs from the ovaries and freezing them for a future pregnancy.

This week, Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced she too was beginning the process of freezing her eggs, documenting the daily mechanics of giving herself hormone shots on social media.

News.title: People who fled Stourbridge fires start to return home
News.content:
People who had to flee their houses during the devastating Stourbridge fires are starting to return home, as a firefighter said it was "a miracle no one has died".

Many families are only just discovering the extent of damage to their homes as West Midlands Fire Service allowed some behind the cordon after three days.

Nineteen properties across five streets have been fully destroyed. Eight households have been able to view the shells of their former homes.

Aerial images of the scene appear to show some houses have remained entirely intact while those next to them have been burnt to the ground.

Residents of Brunswick Gate, Landsgate, Ounty John Lane, Quarry Park Road and Racecourse Lane were asked to gather to speak to fire chiefs one by one.

They then learned if it was safe to return or if their home needed significant repairs or had been lost entirely.

Earlier, Dudley Council's chief executive Balvinder Heran said 96 evacuated houses had escaped damage with 85 families able to return.

Thirteen households whose properties were damaged by fire have also been able to go back home.

News.title: UK-made drones strike targets inside Russia
News.content:
British-made drones are being used to strike targets in Russia for the first time.

The drones, built by two separate British companies, have been used in mainland Russia in widespread and successful targeting of military and industrial targets, including refineries and warehouses of online retailer Wildberries.

The strikes, first reported by the Sunday Times, external, are said to have caused more than Â£35bn in economic damage. A well-placed military source confirmed to the BBC the UK drones had been used.

British manufactured Storm Shadow missiles had earlier been used in the conflict, although this new phase is having a far more decisive impact.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has previously said drones using UK components and configurations have been used to attack Russian territory, including a fuel depot in the Kamensky District of the Rostov Region.

In April, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) announced it would supply Ukraine tens of thousands of drones, including long-range strike devices, in its biggest ever package.

The MoD said its support for Ukraine is "unwavering" and would stand by its ally "until it wins".

A spokesperson said: "We are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin's illegal invasion.

"This includes over 150,000 drones this year, cutting-edge Stone Cloak devices that hinder Russian air defences and innovative low-cost cruise missiles."

On Sunday, Moscow's mayor said about 600 Ukrainian drones were launched towards the city overnight, with roughly a third of the drones being destroyed, and three people were injured.

A warehouse belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries was hit.

Wildberries, known as Russia's version of Amazon, has been repeatedly targeted since July.

Kyiv said at the time it was targeting logistics hubs used by Russians to buy military equipment and disrupting supplies to the Russian army.

News.title: Soldiers praised for 'phenomenal job' helping crews tackle wildfires
News.content:
In south Wales, about 14 separate fires were being tackled by crews on Sunday.

Mid and West Wales Fire Rescue and Service said crews were dealing with blazes at Rhandirmwyn and Ammanford in Carmarthenshire and Hay-on-Wye and Brecon in Powys on Sunday.

They have also attended fires in Gorseinon, Swansea, and Tenby, Pembrokeshire, as well as an incident involving smoke in Llanelli, Carmarthenshire.

Fire service manager, Geraint Thomas, described tree-height flames spreading in a pine forest in the Rhandirmwyn area of Carmarthenshire.

He said the perimeter of the fire expanded to 480 hectares with areas of broadleaved woodland, mountain moorland as well as pine forest burning within it.

"It's really challenging terrain in places," he said.

"The majority of the fire is quite deep-seated in the pine forest. We were limited in what we could see."

The Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service area manager said the flames are now under control thanks largely to much cooler conditions on Friday.

Chris Bryant, MP for Rhondda and Ogmore, said a fire in Treherbert, Rhondda Cynon Taf, had been "appalling" and he thanked crews from London who had provided assistance.

"Thankfully, there are fire engines from all over the UK and two helicopters have been in place all afternoon.

"I'm immensely impressed by the fire workers. But this can't be our new normal," he said, in a post on X, external on Saturday.

Monahan praised the Royal Logistics Corps and Royal Engineers in ensuring crews had water to tackle the fires.

"The Welsh water system is under pressure, so they're moving vast quantities of water from areas that we have it into areas where we're fighting the fire, so that we don't put too much pressure on the water system," he said.

"That's something people probably aren't aware of."

He also said the national emergency fire alert issued by the UK government to people's mobile phones in England and Wales on Friday was "absolutely necessary".

But he expressed disappointment that some people still did not appreciate the dangers.

"Even after that transmission, I stopped and found someone who was burning tyres underneath a tree.

"This is irresponsible behaviour," he said.

News.title: Sinn Féin condemn burning of images of first minister on Derry bonfire
News.content:
Sinn FÃ©in has condemned the burning of images of First Minister Michelle O'Neill on a bonfire in Londonderry as "anti-democratic" and "sectarian".

On Saturday, a bonfire, from which almost 500 pallets were removed during the week, was set on fire beside a road in the Bogside area.

Photos of O'Neill, as well as union jacks, Israeli flags, Parachute Regiment, Somme Remembrance and Northern Ireland flags were attached to the bonfire.

Police are treating the burning of the effigies and materials as sectarian-motivated hate crimes.

In a post on social media, O'Neill said she would "not be deterred, distracted or intimidated".

"I will continue to call out sectarianism, anti-community activity and destruction wherever it comes from.

"These bonfires are a blight on our community," she said.

Secretary of State for Northern Ireland Sir Chris Bryant said it was "wrong and I strongly condemn it".

"Hatred like that only takes us back to the past - which is not what the vast majority of people in Northern Ireland want."

North Belfast MP John Finucane said these bonfires were "hate filled sectarianism" and "the very antithesis of Irish republicanism".

Youths placed pallets near the bottom of the Lecky Road flyover and set fire to it just before 23:00 BST.

Two other bonfires in the Creggan and Top of the Hill areas of the city also had flags and effigies placed on them before being set alight.

News.title: Elgin man found after going missing in Rome on first night of holiday
News.content:
A 56-year-old man from Moray who went missing in Rome on the first night of his holiday has been found, according to his family.

Colin Ross had just arrived in the Italian capital with partner Anabella Mcallister, when he disappeared up a side street near the Pantheon at about 22:00 on Friday evening.

Posting on social media, Mcallister said Ross, from Elgin, had become unsteady due to his medication and the heat, and did not have his phone or wallet with him.

His daughter later told STV News, external that he'd been found injured "walking around in the street" but "somehow made it back".

After Ross went missing, Mcallister said online that "he was in a bit of an unsteady state due to medication and heat."

She added that as she stopped to take a photograph, her fiancÃ© went up a side street and by the time she had followed him he had disappeared.

Earlier, a spokesperson for the Foreign Office said it was supporting the family of a British man missing in Italy and was in touch with the local authorities.

BBC Scotland News has contacted Italy's state police for comment.

News.title: Man with dementia given days to leave Sweden
News.content:
Torossian said the situation had been "awful" and "traumatic" for the family.

"I'm just worried that if the police go in and try and take him, how is that going to affect my dad. We just want him to have some dignity," she said.

"We want him to be treated like someone - he's very vulnerable, and I just feel that this is really ruthless and harsh."

Torossian said doctors had advised the Swedish authorities the process of moving Mason to the UK would pose a "danger to his life".

When the UK left the European Union (EU) on 31 January 2020, British citizens stopped being EU citizens, which meant they could no longer stay in Sweden with right of residence status.

During a transitional period, British citizens could apply for residence status under a withdrawal agreement between the UK and the EU - which ended on 31 December 2021.

Torossian explained due to Mason's health conditions, a 'god man' - a legally appointed trustee - was given power of attorney to look after her dad's affairs.

Documents from the Swedish Migration Agency, seen by the BBC, state an application for permanent residency for Mason was made on 21 December 2021.

However, it was refused on the grounds documents showing he met the grounds for residency were not submitted.

News.title: Belgian Pocognoli confirmed as Scotland boss
News.content:
The Scottish FA say they have appointed "one of Europe's brightest emerging coaching talents" by securing Sebastien Pocognoli as Scotland men's new head coach on a two-year deal.

The 39-year-old Belgian, who replaces Steve Clarke, left Monaco at the end of last season and previously led Union Saint-Gilloise to a first league title in 90 years in 2024-25.

He becomes just the second foreign boss of the Scotland men's team, after German Berti Vogts.

"When I first heard of the interest, I was immediately excited about the opportunity," said former Belgium international Pocognoli.

"Scotland's supporters are famous for their passion - most recently at the World Cup in the USA - and I have experienced it myself as a player for Belgium when we played in 2013.

"Along with my coaching staff, I will do everything I can to give them a team to be proud of and build on the success that has been achieved already by my predecessor.

"Since negotiations began, I have been doing a lot of research, asking a lot of questions and looking at areas that we can build on."

News.title: Parents 'watering down baby milk' over high costs
News.content:
A baby bank says parents are turning to "unsafe" practices such as watering down baby formula milk to save money.

Megan Sinden, founder of Moorside Baby Bank in Consett, County Durham, said a couple of families spoke of putting less powder in to get another week's worth out of it, "which to me is quite dangerous".

She called for a cap on rising costs of formula, saying: "It's not a luxury item, it's a basic need for a baby."

Charity National Childbirth Trust (NCT) said its recent study found nearly half of parents (48%) were struggling more financially after having a baby, and added infant formula should always be prepared according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Infant formula is designed to provide the correct balance of nutrients for babies when mothers cannot or choose not to breastfeed, and adding extra water alters that balance.

The lower concentration can cause nutrient deficiency, coupled with the reduced ability of the baby's body to absorb the nutrients, NCT said.

"In turn, this can lead to poor weight gain, growth problems, and developmental delays," the spokesperson said.

"In serious cases, too much water in the formula may lead to more immediate health problems because a baby's body is not able to safely process the excess water."

The latest report, external by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) found the average retail price of some infant formula had increased by more than 25% in recent years.

Moorside Baby Bank opened in February 2025 and has so far helped 226 families with goods like clothes, nappies and baby wipes, which were mainly donated by the community.

Sinden, who is a community worker from nearby Stanley, said the bank struggled to get donations of baby milk "because it is so expensive" and instead relied on grants to buy the formula in.

World silver 200m medallist Amy Hunt sealed an unprecedented quadruple on a six-medal final day for Great Britain at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.

Hunt became the first athlete to win four gold medals at a single European championships after Jeremiah Azu, Dina Asher-Smith, Zharnel Hughes and Hunt triumphed in the mixed 4x100m relay at the Alexander Stadium.

Asher-Smith also moved to the outright top of the European Athletics Championships all-time list with her 11th medal, and silver for Matt Hudson-Smith in the men’s 4x400m relay, bringing the hometown hero to nine, made him the outright most-decorated man in the history of the European Championships.

open image in gallery Amy Hunt celebrates after winning her fourth gold medal (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

Georgia Hunter Bell won 1500m gold, there was a pair of silvers in the women’s 4x400m relay and for Jazmin Sawyers in the long jump, and Abbie Donnelly became the first British woman to win a marathon medal at the European Championships, with bronze.

The mixed 4×100 relay made its European Championships debut in Birmingham, opening the possibility for the ambitious Hunt to set her sights on four titles on home soil.

“Oh my gosh, I’m over the moon,” Hunt told the BBC. “And I think to finish it off with some of my best friends in the sport, me and Jeremiah actually have the same birthday so we’re kind of twins.

“To do it all together is incredible, especially because that was the first time we kind of did that changeover about an hour ago in warm-up.

“First time ever – and look how smooth it was. Such professionals. It was a bit like, you know when you’re queuing for a rollercoaster and you’re like a little bit nervous and you’re seeing the drops and stuff, and then when you get off you want to do it again? It was that adrenaline kick certainly. I loved the event.”

open image in gallery Georgia Hunter Bell crosses the line to win gold in the 1500m (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

Hunt, the 2025 world 200m silver medallist, wrapped up the sprint double before winning gold with the women’s 4x100m relay quartet on Saturday night, then the mixed team beat Germany and Spain in 39.97 seconds.

Asher-Smith joined Polish sprinter Irena Szewinska on 10 European medals with women’s 4×100 relay triumph on Saturday after also collecting 200m bronze earlier in the week, although she already had two more golds to her name.

With Sunday’s addition, the British record-holder is now up to eight European golds, and is the lone athlete with 11 medals overall.

Hunter Bell, the Paris 2024 Olympic bronze medallist at 1500m and Tokyo 2025 world silver medallist at 800m, beat Poland’s Klaudia Kazimierska and Patricia Silva of Portugal to seal the third senior title of her career in four minutes, 7.78s.

open image in gallery Abbie Donnelly with her bronze medal (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

Charlie Dobson nearly staged a final-leg comeback, but the British quartet of Hudson-Smith, Toby Harries, Ben Jeffries and Dobson finished three one hundredths of a second behind Italy in the competition’s closing race.

There was also silver for their counterparts, Yemi Mary-John, Lina Nielsen, Nicole Yeargin and Emily Newnham in three minutes, 21.68s, as well as long jumper Sawyers, with a best-effort 6.99m.

Donnelly took home marathon bronze in two hours, 27 minutes and 33 seconds.

News.title: ‘Obsessed’ killer talked about murdering his ex for months before carrying out the crime, cops say
News.content:

A Connecticut man spent months talking about killing his ex-girlfriend before stabbing her to death in her apartment, according to police.

New Haven Police Department officers arrested 41-year-old Matthew Almontes after responding to a distress call Wednesday from Tisha Marinoccio, 41.

Marinoccio contacted authorities to report that her ex-boyfriend had stabbed her inside her apartment and fled with the weapon. Emergency responders transported her to a hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Almontes faces charges of murder and tampering with evidence. He remains in custody on a $1.5 million bond and is scheduled to make a court appearance on Aug. 26.

Police records obtained by the New Haven Register reveal that an employee at the 300 block Orange Street apartment complex — where both Almontes and Marinoccio lived in separate units — reported that Almontes had talked about stabbing the victim over the course of six months. The worker informed investigators that Almontes had grown obsessed with Marinoccio and was experiencing “mental deterioration.”

open image in gallery Matthew Almontes, 41, faces murder and evidence tampering charges in connection with the fatal stabbing of Tisha Marinoccio, according to the New Haven Police Department ( New Haven Police Department )

Two days before to the killing, Almontes made a direct threat to the building employee, the New Haven Register reported.

“I’m going to kill her,” Almontes allegedly told the worker Monday. “I’m gonna stab her and they're not gonna find a weapon.”

Following the attack, police found Almontes nearby and took him into custody. Investigators reviewed security camera footage from the property, which showed the suspect “entering and exiting the victim's apartment as well as exiting the rear of the apartment building, where he discarded an unknown object inside the rear-alley dumpster.”

Officers later recovered the knife used in the attack inside that dumpster, according to police statements.

“Upon arrival, they located Marinoccio inside her apartment suffering from a stab wound,” the department stated.

Almontes declined to speak with investigators after his arrest.

Georgia Hunter Bell has taken inspiration from her compatriots when it comes to being open with her targets and she now has just one major victory this year to tick off.

The 32-year-old provided her latest tactical masterclass to win her maiden European gold on the final night in Birmingham, biding her time before producing a devastating kick with 150m remaining.

The chasing pack had no answer and Hunter Bell crossed the lines with arms outstretched as she added to the World Indoor and Commonwealth crowns she already has to her name in 2026.

“Going into things as the favourite and delivering is hard,” said Hunter Bell, who will bid to complete a golden year at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest next month.

“It’s much harder than going in as an underdog. It means a lot to prove to yourself you can do it as well as everyone else. I’ve been embracing the pressure and thinking let’s just go for it.

“Everyone knows I want to win, I know I want to win, I’m going to put my goals out there now.

“I’m really inspired by what Josh Kerr has done this year and the way he has spoken about it, Amy (Hunt) as well, saying what she wants to do.

“I really love how everyone in British athletics is pushing the bar up. We are in a fun era.”

open image in gallery Georgia Hunter Bell celebrates with the British flag ( Reuters )

Hunter Bell is blessed with an intriguing choice ahead of her as she weighs up her journey to LA 2028.

Her recent Commonwealth triumph and last year’s World Championship silver came over two laps and she could add further competition to a field including Hodgkinson, Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol if she prioritises the shorter distance.

But this performance showed she is equally at home over the longer trip, while she has not ruled out attempting to emulate Kelly Holmes’ achievements from Athens 2004 and doubling up.

“There’s still a lot left of this season,” she said. “I haven’t done a paced 800m yet and I’ve got one coming up with all the speedy girls so I’m looking forward to throwing my hat in the ring there.

“I had a bit of FOMO when I saw them on the podium but it’s such an exciting time. I’m just really happy.”

Life in the real world has equipped Hunter Bell with a perspective that means she doesn’t take these moments for granted.

Her role in cyber-security also provided useful preparation when it comes to coping with pressure while methodical planning is bearing fruit.

open image in gallery Georgia Hunter Bell celebrates as she crosses the finish line ( Reuters )

“We always go through everything,” she said. “Jen (Meadows) quizzes me and says if it gets like this, what would you do.

“A lot of the time the race doesn’t go how we planned but because we’ve done the preparation, we are ready to adjust however it goes.

“When I came out, I wanted to embrace the crowd but didn’t want to get swept up in the occasion, so I was all business. But I ran it logically and in the final few steps, I allowed myself to soak up the emotion and really feel it.

“That last 150m is always my favourite part of the race and it was really nice to come down the home stretch and know I had it. I’m really hoping to make it four in September.”

Elizabeth Olsen has reportedly welcomed her first child with her husband, musician Robbie Arnett.

The 37-year-old Wandavision star and her 34-year-old partner were photographed together in Los Angeles, with Olsen wearing the infant in a white baby carrier.

Page Six reports that the couple were spotted out and about with the child on Saturday, August 15.

Olsen and Arnett met while on vacation in Mexico in 2017, and the Marvel star later confirmed that they had married in a private ceremony “before Covid.” Arnett is a multi-instrumentalist known for his work with the indie band Milo Greene.

Olsen is the younger sister of former child stars Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, and has previously spoken out about whether she would let her own children act from a young age.

open image in gallery Elizabeth Olsen and her husband Robbie Arnett, pictured in 2023, have reportedly welcomed their first child ( Justin Shin/Getty Images for Gucci )

In a 2023 interview with The Times, the actor admitted she was reluctant to allow any of her children to act professionally before they turn 18.

“Hard no,” she told the interviewer with a laugh. Her elder twin sisters, however, began their first job at nine months old, sharing the role of Michelle Tanner on the family sitcom Full House.

Olsen went on to clarify that her decision has less to do with Mary-Kate and Ashley’s specific experiences, and more to do with the existing difficulties of navigating modern life as a young person.

“My sisters are unique so it’s not a reflection on them when I say no, I think it’s a reflection more on culture today,” she said.

“Being younger today is already so complicated. To amplify it by being a child actor and then amplify it by social media, I just think it’s a lot for a kid’s development... I think my sisters are on a totally different path than your average child actor.”

open image in gallery Ashley, Elizabeth and Mary-Kate Olsen in 2016 ( Getty Images )

Ashley retired from acting in 2004, with Mary-Kate following in 2012. Since 2006, the sisters have both had successful fashion careers after founding New York-based luxury brand, The Row.

Previously, Elizabeth shared her feelings about growing up with media attention as the sister of the Olsen twins and an actor in her own right.

“It’s weird growing up with that,” Olsen told singer Jessie Ware and her mother Lennie on their Table Manners podcast in 2021.

“The paparazzi part was the strange part because they follow you, and as a child it was very scary. They were obsessed with them turning 18.”

News.title: ‘Dreams do come true’: Amy Hunt makes history with fourth gold at European Athletics Championships
News.content:

Amy Hunt is officially a history-maker and a record-breaker for good measure too.

Hunt joined forces with Jeremiah Azu, Dina Asher-Smith and Zharnel Hughes to scorch to mixed 4x100m gold in a new European record of 39.97sec.

She becomes the first athlete to win four golds at the same European Athletics Championships after her success in the 100m, 200m and women’s sprint relay.

Relay running is all about timing and trust, but the mixed event, which makes its Olympic debut in Los Angeles, is new on the programme and presents a unique technical challenge.

Differences in speed, stride length and acceleration between male and female athletes make the changeovers particularly difficult to perfect.

But despite limited practice time, Hunt waited, heart in mouth, on the anchor leg and then powered down the home straight to hold off a fast-finishing Germany in a thriller.

open image in gallery The British quartet celebrate after victory in Birmingham ( Reuters )

"Four golds was the dream and perhaps dreams do come true," said Hunt.

"I don’t think I can begin to communicate what it means. It’s so beyond the bounds of my dreams that I’m just euphoric right now. I can’t believe it’s happening.

"I think it will sink in later, maybe on the podium, I don’t know. I’m just so proud of myself and the way I’ve handled this week — the emotions, the recovery and being strict and staying disciplined after all the highs. I’ve stayed true to myself and true to the job I came out here to do.

"I'll never forget this week and to finish it off with my best friends in the sport is so special.

"We'd not worked on these changeovers until about an hour ago and we were so smooth. I can't wait to see where we take this event.

"It was like queueing for a rollercoaster — you are just so nervous, but when you're done you want to do it all over again."

Hunt, 24, writes a new chapter in the sport and so does Asher-Smith. No athlete has ever won more medals at the European Championships — 11 and counting, with eight of them gold.

"When I started in this sport, all I wanted to be was fast," said Asher-Smith.

"I’m incredibly humbled and grateful to be in this position and still medalling 12 years after my European debut and 13 years after my senior debut as a 17-year-old."

open image in gallery Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith enjoy their victory ( Reuters )

Hunt's next challenge will be to take her European domination and translate it onto the global stage.

Her 200m world silver last year shows what's possible, but there are 13 faster athletes in the world this season over the distance and 24 in the 100m.

However, her regular racing schedule in both events means she has a world ranking that should secure an invite to the £7m World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest next month.

And that will be a gilt-edged chance to test where she stands ahead of next year's Worlds in Beijing and, beyond that, LA, which she makes no secret is her North Star ambition.

"We're the best sprint nation in Europe, we've cleaned up, but we want to be the best in the world too," added Hunt.

"It’s just euphoric. We all push each other on. When you see other people winning medals, you want to get out there and get a bit of that for yourself.

"It just shows the strength that British athletics has right now. We’re entering this era of dominance."

Great Britain end these championships having won every individual and relay title except the men's 200m, where Hughes was denied by Germany's Owen Ansah, racing under the shadow of a potential four-year ban for allegedly failing to comply with a doping test.

Hughes's upgrade may yet come, but he's excited about what this mixed sprint team, overseen by Olympic medallist Richard Kilty, can do with more time to shave hundredths off their new record by drilling their changeovers.

open image in gallery Zharnel Hughes hails four-time gold medallist Amy Hunt ( Reuters )

"It's all so new and I can only imagine how much better we can get at it," he said. "We only practised it tonight.

"It’s definitely an event that’s going to be spectacular in the future. I’m looking forward to doing it again. We've got a really exciting two years ahead with these guys."

Birmingham has been conquered. Now Hunt and Britain's sprint stars have two years to prove they can rule the world in LA.

Novuna is the Official Finance Partner of British Athletics and proud sponsor of the GB & NI Athletics Team. From everyday goals to world-class dreams, Novuna backs the ambition of millions across the UK — from supporting British businesses and individuals’ plans, to powering British Athletics on the global stage. Find out more at www.novuna.co.uk

News.title: CEO who went viral for firing 900 employees on Zoom before Christmas is now mad that he got fired
News.content:

The CEO of Better Homes & Finance — who notoriously laid off 900 employees on a company Zoom call before Christmas in 2021 — says he feels tricked, as he was just fired and replaced.

Vishal Garg, who made headlines in 2021 for the cruel firings of hundreds of employees at the digital mortgage company, was let go from Better, which he founded and led as CEO, on August 3, CNN reported.

Hedge fund manager Daniel Lewis was then immediately named as the company’s interim CEO — even though he had only been brought onto the board a week earlier. Within that week, Garg says that Lewis convinced the board to oust him. Garg says Lewis then convinced the board to name him as the new CEO.

“He hoodwinked me,” Garg told CNN. “He said he liked the company’s strategy. He praised us on X and used that to get on our board and win our confidences.”

The digital mortgage company had seen numerous setbacks over the years under Garg’s leadership — excluding the catastrophic layoffs, which gained nationwide attention and resulted in the website being flooded with negative reviews.

open image in gallery The CEO of Better.com, known for laying off 900 employees ahead of Christmas in 2021, was recently fired from the company, according to a report ( Getty )

While Better held an $8 million valuation during the COVID-19 pandemic amidst a refinancing boom and low interest rates, it is now valued at only $300 million, according to the report.

Despite the troubles, Garg said he was on the precipice of turning fortunes around for the company. While sales dropped from $1.5 billion in 2021 to $70 million in 2023, this year Better is on pace to deliver $200 million in sales, Garg told the outlet.

That is in part because of its AI models, which it uses to help quickly process mortgages — something that would’ve taken dozens of employees several days to do just years ago.

“We’re winning. We’ve tripled loan volume. We’re close to profitability,” Garg said. “We were at the 5-yard line after taking the ball all the way down the field from the other side.”

Despite his best efforts, Garg said he feels that Lewis convinced the company’s board to get rid of him.

“It’s not about me. I care about delivering savings to people and helping them live the American Dream. So when shareholders said, ‘You need to take a back seat,’ I complied,” Garg said.

open image in gallery Better.com CEO Vishal Garg laid off over 900 employees just ahead of holiday season ( Screengrab/Vimeo/Better.com )

Garg added: “I suspect he always wanted to become CEO. The board made a mistake.”

Investors may agree with Garg’s read on the situation. The company’s stock had fallen 45 percent since Lewis was named as the new CEO.

In the days since, Garg retained a lawyer to try to help him win back his job. He sent a letter to the board on Monday demanding he be reinstated as CEO.

Garg says he will work for $1 a year until Better returns to profitability. Once that goal is reached, he says he will leave the role as CEO.

“It’s an acknowledgement that I’ve been doing this for 10 years, but execution hasn’t been perfect,” he said. “I hope it gets resolved. I think the future still remains very bright for Better.”
