Sports.title: Jacquet scores on debut as Liverpool beat Como
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet was the star as Liverpool enjoyed a confidence-boosting 2-0 win over Como in their final pre-season friendly at Anfield.

The 21-year-old defender was making his debut for the club after signing from Rennes in February and marked the occasion by scoring the second goal just before half-time to double the lead for Andoni Iraola's side after Cody Gakpo had fired in the opener.

Gakpo set up Jacquet for his tap-in which proved to be the final act by the French youngster as he made way for fellow new arrival Ronald Araujo at half-time. The tempo dropped and that suited Como who played more of the football in the second half.

Liverpool had contrived to lose a two-goal lead against Monaco last week but there was no repeat - Ryan Gravenberch even hitting the crossbar late on. As well as Gakpo and Jacquet, Jeremie Frimpong and Rio Ngumoha were among those to impress for Iraola's side.

There are others with work to do. Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz both scored against Monaco, but the former Newcastle striker faded here after a striking a post early on, while the German playmaker flattered to deceive. The real stuff begins next Sunday at St James' Park.

Newcastle United

Liverpool Sunday 23rd August 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Key moments at Anfield

8 - POST! Isak strikes a bouncing ball against the foot of the far post

23 - GOAL! Frimpong brilliantly finds Gakpo to fire Liverpool ahead

44 - GOAL! Gakpo lays the ball across for Jacquet to tap it home

58 - CLOSE! Rodriguez fires a shot into the side-netting for Como

85 - CLOSE! Diao skims the Liverpool crossbar on the counter-attack

89 - BAR! Szoboszlai works it to Gravenberch but he hits the bar

How Jacquet impressed the crowd

Jacquet's name was read out last when the teams were announced as Anfield gave him a special welcome and the young defender responded with a standout performance. The Frenchman certainly pressed his claims for a start against Newcastle next week.

The first cheers for Jacquet came within 30 seconds as a result of a couple of purposeful passes that indicated his willingness to add some drive to a Liverpool backline that was guilty of being a little bit too sluggish on the ball under Arne Slot last term.

And the crowd were chanting his name a quarter of an hour in when he produced a strong challenge right in front of the Kop before doing well to hold off his man in the follow-up tussle for possession. Jacquet looks serene but there is steel there as well.

Image: Jacquet celebrates with Virgil van Dijk after scoring

It was not flawless. He missed a challenge just before the half-hour mark and needed Frimpong to save him with a covering challenge. There was a clumsy miskicked clearance soon after that he made up for with a crucial interception inside the area.

But the goal, tapping in Gakpo's cross, capped off a fine 45 minutes before he was withdrawn at the break. Araujo has been brought in on loan but Jacquet is seen as the long-term solution at the back for Liverpool and this was a very encouraging start.

The statistics show Ibrahima Konate was quick but it could sometimes take a while for the legs to get going. Now 35, Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk needs pace around him in that defence now. In Jacquet, he appears to have found his ideal new partner.

Iraola admits Liverpool 'need to be better'

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola:

On the performance: "We needed this feeling of finishing with a clean sheet and winning the game. Still, the first half has been better than the second but at least we kept our organisation and our composure. We found a way to finish with a clean sheet. We needed this feeling before we started."

"We are better than we were last week. I hope next week we are better than we were today. You can say the first half is still better than the second half, but today a lot of players played 90 minutes and they finished with no cramps.

"It's an improvement but still, especially in the second half, we need to be better.

"We need every player, every time, every minute, every action and that's the commitment. I'm very happy with the attitude of the players. They are training really well. I am asking them to do things that are a little bit different, especially without the ball and I think they are trying to get it.

"We are not perfect. We have things to improve but I'm very happy with their attitude, their willingness to be on the same page and we will get there."

On Jeremy Jacquet: "Jeremy played really well, also Ronald played really well when he came in.

"Also, a very good performance of Jeremie Frimpong, also playing 90 minutes as a right-back helping us offensively but closing very well his side also. Some good performances at the back."

What's next?

Sports.title: West Ham blow two-goal lead at Burnley to draw on Championship return
Sports.content:
Zian Flemming struck twice late on as Burnley came back to deny West Ham in a 2-2 Championship draw between the freshly relegated sides at Turf Moor.

West Ham, strong favourites to make an immediate return to the Premier League, looked set for three points when Manor Solomon rifled home in the 72nd minute, doubling the lead given to them by Max Kilman 10 minutes in.

But Burnley kept scrapping, and Flemming struck an 83rd-minute penalty before finding the net in stoppage time to give his boss Nicky Hayen a first league point on his 46th birthday, and prevent what would have been their first home Championship defeat since April 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Zian Flemming struck a stoppage-time equaliser

West Ham may have lost Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for big transfer fees since the drop, but have crucially kept Jarrod Bowen and this week broke the Championship transfer record with a £22m deal for Arne Engels to underline their promotion credentials.

It was too soon for Engels to be involved here, but for much of the afternoon Nuno Espirito Santo's side looked to have the edge in quality against a Burnley team who too often made the wrong decision and wasted first-half opportunities.

There was less than a minute gone when Flemming flicked over from Jacob Bruun Larsen's cross, but it was a false dawn for Burnley as West Ham scored from their first real chance.

Kilman took advantage of poor defending, easily peeling away from Aaron Ramsey to head in Bowen's free-kick for his first goal in 68 West Ham appearances.

With former manager David Moyes watching on, West Ham were bossing possession as a full away end dominated the atmosphere at Turf Moor, with plenty of bright touches from Solomon - a key part of Leeds' promotion campaign two years ago.

Burnley had the momentum at the start of the second half, but Flemming had already wasted two excellent chances before he got above Konstantinos Mavropanos to send Marcus Edwards' inswinging cross onto the post, from where it bounced back into the arms of a grateful Mads Hermansen.

Flemming's frustration then grew as another effort was cleared off the line by Ollie Scarles from Bruun Larsen's corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Debutant Manor Solomon doubled West Ham's lead

West Ham's first shot of the second half did not come until the 71st minute when Bowen's strike hit his own man in Kilman, but Burnley never fully cleared it and Mohamadou Kante danced down the touchline before his cross was deflected for Solomon to lash home.

But Burnley got a lifeline when Scarles scythed down Edwards in the box and Flemming sent Hermansen the wrong way, and two minutes into the seven added on, the ball broke to him following a scramble in the box and he picked out the bottom corner.

Nuno eyes attacking signings | 'Draw tough to take'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Kilman opened the scoring for West Ham

West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo speaking to Sky Sports on whether he wants to sign a striker:

"Yeah, unfortunately today Pablo felt something in the calf. We need more options in the offensive part of the team, of course."

On the draw: "It was a tough one to take. First half, we did things quite well. We controlled, we played good, we created a lot of situations.

"Second half, Burnley reacted, had a couple of chances, but after we scored the second time it was about trying to keep the result, having more of the ball. We were not able to do as much as we should.

"We should have kept the ball more and tried to exploit a little bit more of the space that we had. But overall, the result, the chances of Burnley, ourselves, we have to be fair."

Hayen: It feels like we won the game

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Flemming pulled one back from the spot

Burnley boss Nicky Hayen speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm really pleased with the way we showed resilience and came back in a game that we actually didn't deserve to lose.

"The team showed character today, and that's the most important. They were really clinical, and we weren't.

"At the end, we level up, and it gives a feeling that you won the game, even if we have one point.

"But the way we came back was really good, and I'm really pleased for everyone.

"When you draw against one of the biggest favourites for the title, you can be happy."

'Draw magnifies West Ham's need for a new forward'

Ex-West Ham goalkeeper Rob Green speaking to Sky Sports on the Hammers' pursuit of Leeds forward Joel Piroe:

"Bring him in, and today just really magnified that they need it.

"Pablo, for all his endeavour, he's not scored a goal yet for the club. They had two shots on target today.

"He's not creating anything, so you're looking for a guy to add goals, add more creation and someone who's a target and a force to be reckoned with.

"The season's so long in the Championship, and Nuno knows this, as he alluded to himself - more options. It was plural.

"The cynic in me says this was a good day for Nuno because he turns around and bang, that's where we're short."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Middlesex stun Durham to deny Stokes spot in One-Day Cup final
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes and Durham were denied a spot in the 2026 Metro Bank One-Day Cup final as Middlesex pulled off a stunning, comeback clinch a first List-A final appearance for 36 years.

Middlesex appeared to be headed for a heavy defeat when reduced to 145-7 in the 31st over of their semi-final, chasing 255 to win - Colin Ackermann claiming 3-46 - but Luke Hollman's magnificent, unbeaten 83 steered the home side to a memorable two-wicket win.

Hollman shared in a pivotal 79-run partnership with Tom Helm (40) for the eighth wicket, before Noah Cornwell (1no) hung around as Hollman ticked off the final 31 runs required to clinch victory with eight balls to spare.

Sports.title: ‘That’s the standard’: Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal’s desire on blue day for Maresca
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players demonstrated their hunger to defend the Premier League title in their Community Shield triumph over Manchester City. Arsenal, who ended their 22-year wait last season and are seeking to win back-to-back top-flight titles for the first time since 1934-35, beat City 3-0 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff in Enzo Maresca’s first significant match in charge.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after 24 seconds, the fastest goal in the competition since Bobby Owen’s strike for City in 1968, before Kai Havertz doubled Arsenal’s lead and their captain, Martin Ødegaard, completed the scoring on 48 minutes. The 3-0 defeat represented the joint-heaviest loss for a City manager in their first game in charge, with Harry Newbould the most recent to suffer a three-goal opening defeat – 4-1, also to Arsenal, in 1906. It is also Maresca’s joint-heaviest defeat as a manager in England.

Arteta was delighted with Arsenal’s convincing display. “I am obviously extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” he said. “We talked about the desire we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it and I saw a lot of positive things against a top opponent. I’m very impressed in the manner that we played, in the manner that we competed. That’s the standard for us. If we drive the standards at this level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really, really competitive.”

Asked about the desire displayed by his team, he said: “Because we want to go straight again. The desire comes [because] I want to live that moment again. I want to live other moments, even bigger than them … we know what it’s going to take. We know the difficulty of the task. We’ve never done it at this club, to win it again. We know that it’s going to demand something special and we are ready for it.”

Arteta praised the performance of Christos Tzolis, who was involved in all three goals. “He is a really intelligent boy and he has a massive quality, which is when he is in the last 20-30m [of the pitch] he is so composed to pick people out in and around the box,” said the Arsenal manager. “And also to finish actions and he has shown that again two or three times. He was decisive.”

View image in fullscreen New signing Christos Tzolis was involved in all three of Arsenal’s goals. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

Ødegaard said the team’s performance was evidence they are capable of winning back-to-back titles. “We played some brilliant football,” said Arsenal’s captain. “[It was a] great performance and a great way to start the season. I always want to help the team as much as possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals. We showed our level today. We’ve shown we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again. We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again. We want to win everything.”

Maresca acknowledged City, who are closing on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi as they prepare to sell Rodri to Barcelona, would welcome new arrivals before their league opener at home to Bournemouth on Sunday. Rodri did not travel to Cardiff, where Elliot Anderson started in midfield, and Jack Grealish arrived from the substitutes’ bench for his first City appearance since May 2025. “Any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week and if they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better that they can also understand the way we want to play,” he said.

Maresca said he was not alarmed by the manner of the defeat. “In general I’m always concerned, even when we win games so imagine how [concerned] that we didn’t win the game,” said the Italian, who succeeded Pep Guardiola this summer. “It’s just the beginning, we have many things that we need to do better, I think the reaction was good after conceding the first goal and now try to reset and analyse the game and think from Tuesday about the next game.”

Sports.title: Rodri set to complete Barcelona move after Manchester City accept £65.4m bid
Sports.content:
Rodri looks set to complete a move to Barcelona after Manchester City accepted a bid of £65.4m from the Spanish club.

The 30-year-old World Cup winner had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with the Spanish international out of contract next summer.

City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.

Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.

Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the 2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.

City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.

The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says this year is ‘probably’ his last as a footballer
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo believes this year is “probably” his last as a professional footballer, the 41-year-old Portugal captain said in an interview with Vogue magazine published on Sunday.

Ronaldo, who has established his place among football’s all-time greats with more than 950 goals for club and country, had previously spoken of retiring “soon” or within “one or two years”.

“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” the Al-Nassr forward told Vogue, saying his future after football was “all mapped out”.

“I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard,” he said, listing travel and padel among his favourite activities. “Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.”

Ronaldo married his partner, Georgina Rodríguez, in an intimate ceremony in the Portuguese resort of Cascais on Tuesday. The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus player told Vogue he wanted to “continue to enjoy what I’ve earned – what we’ve earned. Because after all it’s been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.”

After being part of the Portugal side which reached the last 16 of the World Cup this summer, Ronaldo is due to link up with Al-Nassr for the new Saudi Pro League season.

Sports.title: Nabizada stunner edges Watford past Southampton as ‘Spygate’ still looms large
Sports.content:
Southampton will have to get used to being barracked as they travel the Championship this autumn, the “Spygate” team set to be everyone’s favourite boo boys in the second tier. Certainly that was the case in Hertfordshire, with Watford fans and players alike beside themselves after a hard-fought victory, decided by two memorable first-half goals.

Tonda Eckert, the Southampton head coach, remains under investigation for his part in the Spygate affair and presented a subdued figure both during and after this contest. He insisted that his team were more united than ever after suffering the indignity of being removed from last season’s playoffs, “but it would be easier to say that after a victory”, Eckert acknowledged.

Watford paid tribute to Kenny Jackett before the match, the one-club legend and local boy hailed with two minutes of applause. This celebration of longevity and connection, with a Panini-inspired tifo tumbling down the stands, cut a contrast with the current operation, where Alessio Dionisi has become Watford’s 12th full-time manager in just the past five years.

“I am very tired and my team was too by the end,” said the Italian who was coaching Empoli in Serie B last season. Dionisi praised the attitude of his team – “I liked the mentality of my players, in every moment I saw one team working together,” he said. He also benefited from the Pozzo family’s multi-club network and the local academy in digging out a victory.

The Spain under-21 attacker Iker Bravo was one of several signings to make the familiar trek from “sister” club Udinese this summer, and he made his mark quickly, opening the scoring with a quite stunning solo goal in the 12th minute. It was all his own work and Bravo had to deploy a combination of skills to turn an innocuous situation into real danger. Looking to latch on to a long ball some 40 yards from goal, the 6ftplaymaker won the first header then, crucially, got a second touch with an outstretched toe to get the ball under control. Bravo then span immediately and drove at goal, pushing his way into the box before chopping right and getting off a low shot that Daniel Peretz got a hand to, butcould not keep out.

View image in fullscreen Watford’s Amin Nabizada jumps for joy after scoring their second goal against Southampton. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA

A great way to start any season, the energy among the Vicarage Road crowd grew immediately and the home side went on to dominate the first half. They doubled their lead in the 29th minute with a moment to remember for 19-year-old academy graduate Amin Nabizada who exploited the same gaps on the left of the Southampton defence to run with the ball from his own half before finishing precisely from a tight angle. “Nabizada was emotional but after the first 10 minutes he played well,” Dionisi said. “When there is one mentality amongst the team, then it’s better for him too.”

Southampton had the better of the second half, taking advantage of a drop in tempo from the hosts to assert their interests. A spell of concerted possession in the 56th minute ended with Kuryu Matsuki pulling out wide, the young midfielder Cam Bragg moving unmarked into the half space and his shift left finding the Canada World Cup star Cyle Larin to poke home from 10 yards out.

Larin had a chance to equalise just two minutes later with a shot on the turn but Federico Ravaglia – another new signing to impress for the Hornets – turned the ball round the post. When Finn Azaz came on as a second-half substitute for the Saints he bought an inch to fire off a low drive that went just beyond the left hand post. As a succession of dangerous set pieces were sent over by Ryan Manning, Southampton fans were singing “we’ll score when we want”.

But as the game passed through a flurry of substitutions Eckert’s team were unable to generate enough momentum to truly unsettle Dionisi’s men. Their only further chance came in added time and was scuffed wide by Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Eckert said he had been happy enough with his team’s performance beyond “two errors in possession”. He insisted his squad are “very close and united” as a group. “We had a different expectation for the result but the group looks united and we now need to turn that into results.”

Opening matches rarely offer much insight into how a season will pan out. But Watford fans were able to enjoy both temperate weather and a decent performance. If Southampton want to transform the negative energy of Spygate into something positive, meanwhile, they will have to start again next week.

Sports.title: Flemming’s dramatic Burnley double pegs back West Ham on Championship return
Sports.content:
There are many good reasons why Burnley and West Ham are performing as Premier League tribute acts, slumming it in the Championship with the hope of a shot at the limelight once more. They are two flawed teams, relegated because of chronic defects, and plenty were on show as West Ham blew a two-goal lead to start life on the second-tier circuit with an entertaining draw.

Zian Flemming’s late double secured a thoroughly deserved point for the hosts, who showed promise going forward but took far too long to find a clinical finish. Despite going two goals ahead through Maximilian Kilman and Manor Solomon, West Ham rarely looked comfortable as they sat back, something that eventually cost them.

“We did a very good first half,” Nuno Espírito Santo said. “We created a lot of situations we were able to control and stop Burnley. Not so good in the second half, but after we scored the second goal, I think we should have done better to keep the result.”

Nuno continued his career-long love of conservatism and his side were put under pressure early on, only surviving through Burnley’s poor decision-making and inept finishing. In addition to continuity in the dugout, West Ham can boast their captain, Jarrod Bowen, who committed to the club rather than seek a quick return to the top flight this summer. It was his corner that found Kilman at the back post after he lost Aaron Ramsey in the box.

Considering West Ham are favourites to go back up, this fortuitous lead should have been a foundation to build on, but little attempt was made to seek a second. They were passive for long periods, composed in possession, but Burnley were able to counter at speed through the midfield and cause problems, only to lack the composure to make the most of those situations.

Nuno tried to rectify the faltering midfield by sending on James Ward-Prowse for the anonymous Pablo, a player who has yet to find his level in England. It made no difference as Burnley came out the better side, pinning West Ham back repeatedly, but Flemming appeared destined to not score, finding the fans, goalkeeper, the inside of the post and Ollie Scarles on the line rather than the back of the net.

West Ham reminded everyone that they possess Premier League quality as Mohamadou Kanté made light work of Marcus Edwards on the right wing before pulling the ball back to Solomon to slam home from close range. This was their second and final shot on target, both leading to goals. Despite being second best, the visitors must have believed they were out of sight, by accident rather than design.

View image in fullscreen Maximilian Kilman gives West Ham the lead as he heads home Jarrod Bowen’s cross. Photograph: COLORSPORT/Alan Martin/Shutterstock

Flemming had other ideas as things finally clicked, aided by Scarles crudely taking out Edwards in the box, allowing the striker to settle his nerves after 83 minutes of near misses and create tension in the West Ham ranks. It worked as the visitors failed to clear a corner which Flemming swept home in the second minute of added time, further explaining why he has attracted transfer interest. Asked if Flemming will stay the Burnley manager, Nicky Hayen, who is desperate not to lose his talisman, said: “It does not help that he scored twice today.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Nuno will want more action in the transfer market after the record Championship signing of Arne Engels from Celtic on Saturday. A striker is much needed as Taty Castellanos made little impact, while the aforementioned Pablo does not give the impression of a man who will fire West Ham to promotion. The bench featured five academy graduates, none of who Nuno felt comfortable bringing on, which says a lot. “The club knows the targets and the needs of the team. [We are] working very hard and trying to get the bodies in as soon as possible,” Nuno said. “We need especially in the offensive part of the team.”

Hayen, celebrating his 46th birthday, took his team on a lap of honour after his first league game in charge as he aims to build a relationship with supporters, who suffered through plenty of unwatchable football under his predecessor. “We showed resilience and that’s why I’m really satisfied for these boys because they worked really hard to change this game around and also how we did it,” Hayen said. “I’m pleased with the fans, how they supported us for 95 minutes. We invested a lot of time before this game into them because what we wanted was really to find the connection with them, that we made the promise that we bring energy into the stadium, that we keep on going for 95 minutes and this is exactly what we did.”

Sports.title: End of an era? South Korea’s sun sets in the Premier League but Japan rise
Sports.content:
It has been a cruel summer for South Korea. The national team crashed and burned at the World Cup, the police are investigating the football association, reports have emerged about bribes paid to foreign referees in 2011 and 2012 and there is a real prospect of the English Premier League being Korean-free for the first time since 2005.

That was when Park Ji-sung signed for Manchester United, to start a love affair between the Land of the Morning Calm and England’s top tier that has continued ever since. Park won four titles and his mantle was taken over in 2015 by Son Heung-min at Spurs.

Son ended his successful decade, during which he became a club captain, by lifting the Europa League in 2025. There are other Taegeuk Warriors who are fondly remembered such as Ki Sung-yueng, Lee Young-pyo and Lee Chung-yong, and then those that would be tougher quiz questions. Cho Won-hee, Yun Suk-young and Park Chu-young barely featured for Wigan, QPR and Arsenal respectively.

Others have cult hero status. Ji Dong-won’s last-minute winner against Manchester City will never be forgotten by Sunderland supporters while Lee Dong-gook, who had a long and successful career, could not hit a barn door with Middlesbrough. While there have inevitably hits and misses, overall, the exports have been a source of pride.

Now, though, those who stayed up late or got up early to watch their compatriots are going to have more free time. After Son left London for Los Angeles, Hwang Hee-chan was the sole participant, but the forward went down with Wolves. There are three Koreans on Premier League books, but Yang Min-hyeok of Spurs, Brentford’s Kim Ji-soo and Park Seung-soo of Newcastle are likely to be once again loaned out.

There was talk of Lee Kang-in leaving Paris Saint-Germain for England, but in July the 25-year-old attacker joined Atlético Madrid to take Antoine Griezmann’s No 7 shirt. The former child TV reality star, introduced to the nation at the age of six and at Valencia’s academy four years later, is now perhaps Asia’s biggest name, but is going to play in England only in Champions League games. At the moment, there are not many other Koreans who look capable of becoming established Premier League players.

That is not the case for Japan, with the Land of the Rising Sun taking the mantle from its eastern neighbour. Last season, Kaoru Mitoma shone with Brighton while there was also Daichi Kamada at Crystal Palace, joined at Selhurst by Takehiro Tomiyasu, Ao Tanaka at Leeds and Wataru Endo with Liverpool.

View image in fullscreen Hwang Hee-chan was relegated with Wolves last season. Photograph: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock

The new season will see more. As Lee was signing for Madrid, Hull snapped up Hidemasa Morita, last seen in England playing for Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League quarter-final against Arsenal in March. Shortly after, Daizen Maeda became Ipswich’s first Japanese player. The forward, who joins after a successful Celtic spell with five league titles, was last in action for Japan against Brazil at the World Cup.

While that game, with the five-time champions coming from behind to win in the 96th minute, was a frustrating one for the Samurai Blue, the team at least did OK. Korea’s World Cup campaign was, however, a disaster with a 2-1 win against Czechia followed by a 1-0 loss by Mexico and a truly dismal defeat by the same scoreline to South Africa. The head coach of the national team and the president of the FA have resigned and Park Ji-sung has been roped in head a new “reform football committee”. It’s a mess.

Park has talked of the need to follow Japan’s long-term philosophy to close the gap with what is clearly Asia’s best team. Increasingly, Japanese players, who have historically headed to Germany first, want to play in England. It is perhaps not a coincidence that two of the promoted Premier League teams have recruited Samurai Blue as there are plenty who have impressed in the Championship in recent years.

It all leads to growing Japanese interest in the Premier League and the opposite in Korea. In 2022, AIA, Tottenham’s shirt sponsor, commissioned a report that claimed there were 12 million fans of the club in the country. Even given Son’s undoubted popularity, wild European claims of fan numbers in Asia have been a feature since before Park arrived at Old Trafford 21 years ago. There are certainly nowhere near 12 million now, with one Korean TV executive saying viewing figures for Spurs games are nowhere near what they were.

That is hardly surprising as widespread Premier League interest in Korea, like Japan, not a historic lover of English football, is still largely player driven. During his time in London, Son’s smiling face would appear in the top corner of the television screen when he was on the pitch to keep casual viewers from turning over. In Park’s time, Manchester United games were often the only one shown all weekend.

When City and the rest of the world were witnessing the Agüero moment in 2012, in Korea, fans had to watch the entirety of United at Sunderland. That was the final sighting of Park in a red shirt and it looks as if Hwang’s appearance against Burnley in May will be the last Korean representation in England’s top tier for some time.

Sports.title: Scotland appoint Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association has appointed the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002 to 2004.

Clarke’s abrupt departure came after Scotland were knocked out of the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager with the Danes Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand being linked with the position.

Pocognoli, a left-back who played for Brighton and West Brom, will probably be welcomed by Scotland fans seeking a fresh approach. Clarke was in position for a generally successful seven years, including appearances at three major tournaments, but was often criticised for a pragmatic style.

Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief football officer, said Pocognoli “will bring an aggressive, front-foot style of play that will excite supporters”.

After a period in youth coaching, Pocognoli enjoyed a successful time in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland. Under Pocognoli, Union won their first title in 90 years in 2025. A move to Monaco followed, but Pocognoli lasted eight months and 38 games in France. The former Everton and Belgum winger Kevin Mirallas is expected to join him in the dugout.

Pocognoli said: “When I first heard of the interest, I was immediately excited about the opportunity. Scotland’s supporters are famous for their passion – most recently at the World Cup in the USA - and I have experienced it myself as a player for Belgium when we played in 2013.

“Along with my coaching staff, I will do everything I can to give them a team to be proud of and build on the success that has been achieved already by my predecessor.”

Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with a trip to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Premier League fans’ previews: our club-by-club guide to 2026-27
Sports.content:
Arsenal

Having finally got the title monkey off our back, and with much of the competition in a state of flux, there’s plenty of optimism. Obviously the target is for Arteta to sustain the same appetite and intensity to mount a credible defence. The big questions are whether we can reproduce the same resilience at the back with Saliba on the long-term missing list, and will the introduction of Guimarães be the catalyst for the sort of midfield chemistry we’ll need to carve open opponents who plan to park the bus?

Key players/weak links On the evidence of our pre-season outings we urgently need the return of our remaining World Cup stars – Rice, Zubimendi and Saka should provide a renewed sense of purpose, both to counter any defensive fragility and to increase our goal threat. We’re all hoping for a breakthrough season for a beefed-up Max Dowman, and are anxious to discover if Tzolis is an upgrade on Trossard.

We still need to sign … Our friendly outings have shown the need for alternative attacking options, such as Atlético’s Julián Alvarez, and cover for Saliba – Quansah and Konsa are linked. But presumably any further arrivals will be dependent on some astute pruning of those who’ve failed to cut the mustard, such as Vieira and Nelson.

Our cult hero is … Benny Blanco’s off-the-ball shenanigans ensure that he’s enshrined as a firm terrace favourite, but it’s the demeanour of Declan Rice that will invariably set the tone for whether or not we’re destined for more success.

If we could sign two players from our past … Who wouldn’t want to add the artistry of Thierry Henry and Dennis Bergkamp to any team?

We will finish 1st. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Chelsea; 3. Manchester City; 4. Liverpool. Bottom three: 18. Coventry; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Sergej Jakirovic.

View image in fullscreen Max Dowman: breakthrough season? Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

Aston Villa

It would be daft to not be optimistic when each year under Emery we’ve created great memories, regardless of the previous summer’s transfer merry-go-round. Top six and a cup run of any flavour would count as a good season, and it may be that our best moments are back-end weighted as we integrate some exciting new talent. I understand that Manzambi is the best thing to come out of Switzerland since the cuckoo clock, and any 22-year-old with 187 senior appearances (Garnacho) must be all right. Perversely, the financial regulations that are holding us back should prevent too much moaning if we don’t get off to a flyer, and having a ground with only three sides might even help us make VP a fortress. In all, I’m fired up for the new season.

Key players/weak links The senior pros all need to keep drinking the Emery Kool Aid, but why wouldn’t they? Konsa remains a colossus and the purple prose around McGinn is fully deserved. If Kamara plays 40 senior games and not his usual 25 it will improve our finishing spot by two. Bournemouth

We’re so looking forward to this: our first ever season in a European club competition. It’s going to be monumental. We still need to sign … Business is pretty much done. We’re in a good place, with maybe one or two to go out on loan deals towards the end of the window.

I’m very optimistic. Twelve months ago we had Yoane Wissa refusing to train to force a move and the footballing world was convinced that our free-kick coach turned manager would get us relegated. Key players/weak links There’s a lot of excitement around new signing Mamadou Sangaré – so much so that he’s already got his own song. Our explosive front three of Ouattara, Thiago and Schade have now had time to gel, and should cause plenty of problems. As for youngsters, 11 players aged 21 or under are vying for a place in the final 25-man squad. 19-year-old striker – and rapper – Kaye Furo is highly rated, as is 20-year-old centre-back Jannik Schuster. We still need to sign … If there’s one position we could strengthen, left-back would be a good option. El Hadji Malick Diouf from West Ham has been rumoured.

Our cult hero is … Michael Kayode. Cemented his status by singing his own terrace chant on camera: “He eats spaghetti, he drinks Moretti, he hates Queens Park Rangers.”

If we could sign two players from our past … We’re probably a bit too “nice”. We will finish 6th. Top four: 1. Manchester City; 2. Arsenal; 3. Manchester United; 4. Bournemouth. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. Brighton

Having seen West Ham, Chelsea and even Crystal Palace go all the way in the Conference League, the main target is doing well in that and winning a first cup final since the 1910 Charity Shield. Am I optimistic about it happening? Not really. The competition looks tougher this year. Freiburg, Atalanta and Monaco all have proper European experience. Even the playoff round against Tromsø is a banana skin. I’m old enough to remember some pretty horrible trips to Carlisle when Brighton could never win north of Lake Windermere. Let alone inside the actual Arctic Circle.

Key players/weak links The key player will be whoever Fabian Hürzeler uses to fill the void left by selling Danny Welbeck: Georginio Rutter, Charalampos Kostoulas or Stefanos Tzimas. Not only did Welbeck score 13 goals last season, but most were vital equalisers or important winners worth 13 points. Allowing him to join Chelsea is a huge risk. If none of those younger alternatives who the club want playing more this season step up and replace Welbeck, there’s the weak link. And there are big question marks over all three.

We still need to sign … Danny Welbeck from Chelsea would be a good signing for his goals record and the experience he would bring to a young squad.

Our cult hero is … Rutter. Nothing says cult hero quite like having one Instagram account about your football career and another about the racehorses you own. With the racing one being more interesting.

If we could sign two players from our past … I’ll spare you another Welbeck answer and say Glenn Murray and Bobby Zamora instead. Hopefully, I’ll be able to revisit this on 3 June 2027 after we’ve just won the Conference League and Kostoulas has hit 46 goals in all competitions. Danny who?

We will finish 13th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester United; 3. Manchester City; 4. Chelsea; Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner.

A new top manager, some decent new signings and a feelgood factor within the squad – it’s hard not to be optimistic. Coventry

There’s no downside to choosing optimism, so yes, we’re optimistic. I don’t expect a top-half finish but I do enjoy how the club’s being run and believe in our ability to compete. Clearly the target is to survive, but within that, if we can showcase what’s good about us and provide a challenge, that would be a very acceptable return.

Key players/weak links The money we’ve spent is basically unfathomable, but my focus has been on those who were so critical to our promotion. Matt Grimes connects everyone in the team so we’re relying on him doing that again, else we’ll have to develop a completely new way to function. Signing keeper Carl Rushworth also gives assurance at the back that we hope will translate into points. There are questions about our strikers (which feels barmy for a team that scored 99 goals last season). It’s not complicated – we simply don’t know if Wright and Simms have what it takes to score at the highest level. Aside from signing Aurèle Amenda, we haven’t touched our defence either. It’s a bold strategy. Liam Kitching and Jay Dasilva have improved significantly, but it’s hard to ignore the notion that we’re relying on players like this finding another uptick. However, new signing Caleb Yirenkyi looks very special.

We still need to sign … We saw how vital Brian Brobbey was for Sunderland last season. A dynamic, high-status striker would go a long way towards calming the nerves about our forward line. Is Taiwo Awoniyi able to be that guy? Let’s hope so. The rumours about Fikayo Tomori are exciting. If we could bring him in, good lord.

Our cult hero is … While the returning Gus Hamer is clearly our cult hero, Milan van Ewijk is the joker of the team. You’ll find him front and centre of every celebration. But don’t let the daftness fool you; he’s a serious, serious player.

If we could sign two players from our past … The original version of James Maddison was unlike anything I’ve ever seen. His game has adapted with age, which is a shame, but I’d love some of that early ingenuity. I’d also welcome back Viktor Gyökeres. He functions far better when he believes he’s the star man. Come home Vik and bash your way to upwards of nine Premier League goals for Coventry.

What are we expecting? Right now, it’s really difficult to say. The only key player to have exited (so far) is Maxence Lacroix, on whom we made a massive profit, but we still have to strengthen the squad so that it can cope with the rigours of going deep in the Europa League without risking our Premier League campaign – a lesson learned from last season. We will finish 14th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Chelsea; 4. Tottenham. Bottom three: 18. Newcastle; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull; First manager sacked Matthias Jaissle.

I’m very optimistic. Sure, chances are that we’ll get relegated but we’ll certainly not be the pushovers people are expecting us to be. Full-back is still a problem position for us: there’s only Ryan Giles on the left and questions over Lewie Coyle and Cody Drameh at this level on the right. We still need to sign … We still really need depth in the full-back areas and desperately need a forward or two to compete with McBurnie. We could do with some more Premier League experience across the back line, too, as well as another back-up goalkeeper thanks to Jack Butland’s lengthy injury.

Our cult hero is … Definitely McBurnie. He’s a handful for every defender and a constant wind-up merchant. The kind of player you hate to be against but love to have in your team.

If we could sign two players from our past … I would have Jarrod Bowen on the wing and Andy Robertson in at left-back. Strangely, they were two transfers I thought might actually happen this summer following West Ham’s relegation and Robertson leaving Liverpool on a free. Alas, it wasn’t to be.
