Our cult hero is … Carrick. He went from being the quiet bloke in the background to dragging United into the Champions League. There’s something very satisfying about a former United player coming back and actually understanding what the club is supposed to be.

If we could sign two players from our past … Robson and Rooney. Captain Marvel in midfield for the leadership, aggression and sheer refusal to accept defeat. Rooney because he was everything you want from a modern forward: technically brilliant, ferocious, selfless and capable of playing anywhere on the pitch.

We will finish 3rd. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Liverpool. Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Leeds; 20. Ipswich. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner: gone before Halloween.

Shaun O’Donnell

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick: cult hero. Photograph: Niall Carson/PA

Newcastle

We’re hurting. We’ve lost our most successful manager in decades, plus his talismanic captain. A-listers have departed and we’ve been humiliated in the transfer market, for the second summer running. Yes, a reset was needed, but we weren’t expecting it to be like this. At least, in Matthias Jaissle, we have a hungry, passionate young manager whose intensity will be welcomed. He certainly looks up for the fight and, despite our outgoings, the German has some exciting talent to work with. According to CEO David Hopkinson, this is “Newcastle United 2.0”. We guess we’ll know what that means in a few months’ time.

Key players/weak links Lewis Miley is “one of our own” and, with Tonali gone, can fulfil his potential. We’ll also be expecting improvements between the posts, with Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen competing for the keeper’s jersey. And if Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga can replicate their World Cup form, we might have a strike force on our hands. The weak links? Joe Willock, who contributed very little to the cause last season and, sadly, Sven Botman, whose form has never recovered from his anterior cruciate ligament injury in 2024.

We still need to sign … A replacement for Bruno Guimarães, leaders on and off the field, high-grade cover at both full-back positions, a centre-half … so not too much to ask … Benfica’s versatile full-back Amar Dedić and Milan’s centre-half Fikayo Tomori would certainly be a good start. Crucially, we need to blend more experience into our youthful side, but any deals will have to be done in stealth mode, given Liverpool’s recent behaviour …

Our cult hero is … Big Dan Burn. A giant of a man, with a heart to match.

If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Shearer for his leadership and goals, and of course, the much-loved, and much-missed, Kevin Keegan. Both knew what it meant to wear the black-and-white shirt.

We will finish 10th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Ipswich; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Álvaro Arbeloa.

David and Richard Holmes

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle: welcome intensity. Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Nottingham Forest

If nothing else, it can’t be as chaotic as last season. We survived fairly comfortably in the end – thanks Vítor! – then sacked him in favour of Glasner, with the rationale being that the Austrian has won silverware. So the target this time isn’t only a decent league finish, but also something in the cabinet.

Key players/weak links The key, like last season, will be Morgan Gibbs-White: the talisman, the on-pitch leader, and the guy who makes things happen for the Reds. After being overlooked for Tommy T’s England squad, he will be keen to continue to show his worth.

We still need to sign … Getting Ousmane Diomande feels important; Murillo and Milenkovic make a great pair but we were still vulnerable in defence last season, and the new guy should balance with the attributes of the established duo. For all that we have loads of wingers, we do desperately need a reliable striker: we can’t continue to rely on a 35-year-old with a chronic knee problem.

Our cult hero is … Fans of other clubs love to take a swipe at our owner, and Reds supporters are frequently quick to jump to his defence. For all the controversies, I genuinely think Marinakis has been great for Forest and for English football: ruthlessly ambitious, aware that decision-making carries risk as well as reward, and unwilling to shrink in the face of so-called “big clubs” or the authorities. He has made some high-profile mistakes but does not shy away from making big calls (sorry Vítor!). And, of course, as Palace fans are aware (along with most of Greece), the Big Guy will also stand up for what he thinks is right and proper, and doesn’t care what other people think.

If we could sign two players from our past … Stan Collymore and Des Walker: pace, power, brilliance.

We will finish 12th. Top four 1. Chelsea; 2. Arsenal; 3. Liverpool; 4. Man United. Bottom three 18. Crystal Palace; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked De Zerbi.

Rich Ferraro, 1865: The Nottingham Forest Podcast

View image in fullscreen Ousmane Diomande: important arrival. Photograph: Lee Keuneke/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

Sunderland

I’m optimistic – but definitely cautiously optimistic. Last season completely exceeded our expectations and finishing seventh with Europa League football on the horizon was incredible. However, Europe changes things. The biggest challenge will be managing the extra games without losing the spark that made us so enjoyable to watch. I’d be very happy with a comfortable mid-table finish and a decent European run. Consolidating ourselves in the league has to be the priority.

Key players/weak links Xhaka is still absolutely pivotal – he brings so much leadership and control – while Le Fée is probably the player I most enjoy watching. I’m also really excited to see what Talbi does this year. He was managed really well last season without too much pressure being put on him, but this feels like his season to really kick on. I don’t think there’s an obvious individual weak link; the concern is whether we have enough depth to compete on multiple fronts.

We still need to sign … I’d still like another attacking option, ideally someone who can play on the right and offer genuine end product. Geny Catamo is an interesting link, but I know the club won’t move unless the figures line up. More than anything, I want quality depth. We could play a ridiculous number of games this season, so we need options rather than simply another big name.

Our cult hero is … Wilson Isidor without question. His “football is life, Sunderland is life” clip probably summed it up perfectly. He gets the club and we genuinely love him. Add in the personality, the goals and his ability to do something brilliant or completely chaotic, and he feels destined to go viral several times this season.

If we could sign two players from our past … Kevin Phillips is the obvious first choice. Put peak Phillips alongside Brobbey and you’ve got a ruthless finisher playing off someone who can hold the ball up and occupy defenders. My second would be Amad. He’d give us quality, creativity and unpredictability out wide, and after how loved he was during his loan spell, bringing him back would feel like a proper homecoming. Put Amad on the wing with Phillips and Brobbey through the middle and I’d be getting dangerously carried away very quickly.

We will finish 12th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Sergej Jakirovic.

View image in fullscreen Wilson Isidor: ‘Sunderland is life’. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

Tottenham

Nothing screams more “Tottenham Hotspur” than stating we’re going to have an outstanding season having finished 17th twice in succession and narrowly avoided relegation. We probably should have gone down. Somehow West Ham managed to be a little bit more rubbish than a team that could barely win home games. Roberto De Zerbi and Enic’s personality change (spending money on end products) is why I’m flirting with the idea of a top-five finish. Absolute greed on my part, but it’s fun to believe. Top eight would be grand.

Key players/weak links Still work to do, but the backline has been rebooted and Micky van de Ven has signed a new contract. In midfield, with Tonali and Fernandes (two of the best mids available to sign) and with Kudus and Deki to return, we finally have depth and quality and strength. The aim will be to galvanise and rejuvenate our home form and regain that confidence and swagger. The key is De Zerbi. His appointment has changed everything. As for youngsters, Luca Williams-Barnett has all the potential to be something special.

We still need to sign … We’ll need plenty done over the next few windows, but ideally, we could do with a winger (we’ve been chasing Savinho for what feels forever) plus a No 10 and a forward. Maddison getting injured again is a concern. We need more than just Solanke up top, with Richy likely to leave.

Our cult hero is … Djed Spence for his World Cup heroics – but we are selling him to Inter. So it has to be the Spurs social media team, the togetherness vibe is the feelgood cleansing we need.

If we could sign two players from our past … It’s a cheat code, but let’s add Harry Kane to the frontline and Gareth Bale to the wing (or any position he wants).

We will finish 17th/1st. Top four: 1. Tottenham; 2. Manchester City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Nottingham Forest; 19. Newcastle; 20. Aston Villa. First manager sacked Mikel Arteta.

Sports.title: Pre-season fight club: How Premier League 'friendlies' became anything but
Sports.content:
As Premier League teams prepare for the fast-approaching 2026-27 season, they've been trudging their way through their customary pre-season friendlies.

This year, however, many of these matches have been anything but friendly, featuring a litany of questionable challenges, red cards and mass confrontations.

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at those in question....

A Spurs scuffle

Sandro Tonali wasted no time demonstrating his competitive spirit in a Spurs shirt during their behind-closed-doors match against Spanish side Getafe.

The Italian, signed in a blockbuster £100m deal from Newcastle this summer, reacted furiously following a late challenge by Getafe's defensive midfielder Mario Martin. Tonali responded to his counterpart's short-sighted attempt at playing the ball by menacingly stalking him up the pitch before landing a few ill-tempered jabs to his chest.

A small scuffle ensued which was quickly broken up by Tottenham stalwart Ben Davies and Tonali's fellow new signings Andrew Robertson and Jan Paul van Hecke.

🎥 Sandro Tonali scuffle in pre-season 🇮🇹 pic.twitter.com/XTGblesDyj — The Spurs Watch (@TheSpursWatch) August 8, 2026

Tonali was left incensed by a challenge from Getafe's Mario Martin, rushing up behind him and shoving him several times, including once to the neck

Several Getafe players rushed towards Tonali and the approaching referee after the incident

Elanga brutally chopped down

Anthony Elanga's pre-season preparations were cut brutally short when the winger was carried off on a stretcher following a terrible challenge from Valencia captain Jose Gaya.

The Spaniard was immediately sent off following the challenge, which sparked a mass confrontation between both sets of players. Elanga was left visibly distressed as he was carried off the pitch, though new boss Matthias Jaissle later provided some relief by confirming that his injury is not quite as serious as first thought.

Following a year in which the majority of the Magpies' star players have been poached, many Newcastle fans are looking to the likes of Elanga to step up as they seek to improve on a dismal 12th place finish last season.

Penalty chaos

Chelsea's Far East tour descended into chaos in Malaysia after striker Liam Delap fell victim to a horror challenge at the behest of Johor Darul Ta'zim defender Antonio Cristian.

In a game with no shortage of shirt pulling, nasty challenges and heated arguments, it was the Spanish defender's reckless attempt to play the ball through his man that saw it reach a boiling point.

Following the full-time whistle, Johor Darul Ta'zim players refused to participate in the penalty shootout that has become customary at the end of many pre-season matches this summer, resulting in a confusing end to a game which featured six goals and seven yellow cards.

Even Chelsea's set-piece coach Austin MacPhee appeared to want a piece of the action, pictured getting into a heated confrontation with a member of the Johor Darul Ta'zim bench as they headed down the tunnel.

A rare friendly red

Bournemouth star Alex Scott and former Manchester United man Antony were both sent off during the Premier League side's clash with Real Betis in southern Spain.

The incident, which began when Colombian midfielder Nelson Deossa rifled the ball at Bournemouth's Bafode Diakite, saw players from both sides embroiled in a fierce confrontation. The confrontation quickly escalated before Scott and Antony were dismissed for aggressively shoving one another. Truthfully, the actions of the two players, who both arrived late to the brawl, were no more egregious than those of their team-mates.

Cherries fans will, however, be thankful that preseason red cards do not constitute a ban in competitive matches and the attacking midfielder will be available to play in Bournemouth's opening Premier League fixture against Manchester City.

‘Tangana’ en el Real Betis-Bournemouth que acaba con las expulsiones directas de Antony y Scott.



Surrealista. pic.twitter.com/yAsIWOzdAP — Gonzalo Tortosa (@GonzaloTortosa) August 8, 2026

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Real Betis' Antony were sent off after a clash during their pre-season friendly

Former Man United winger Antony caused a confrontation between the two teams on the stroke of half-time

Scott was shown a red card for his involvement after he was seen pushing Antony away

Angry Arbeloa

It was new manager Alvaro Arbeloa who saw red in Fulham's penultimate pre-season match on Wednesday.

Following the awarding of a contentious 89th-minute penalty for the hosts, Arbeloa was pictured shaking his head in disbelief on the bench, a stark contrast to the incredulous smiles sported by his players. The Spaniard stormed onto the pitch following the full-time whistle, furiously protested the referee's decision and was promptly dismissed. The Fulham players followed their manager into the dressing room, refusing to take part in the expected penalty shootout and forfeiting the match.

Arriving after a turbulent stint at Real Madrid last season, the Spaniard has seemingly arrived in west London with a point to prove, with many questioning if such an inexperienced manager is the right choice following the high-profile departures of Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez.

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa was sent off after full-time of their 2-2 draw at Malaga

Row between team-mates

Liverpool's stateside pre-season clash with Wrexham devolved into a domestic as several senior players clashed over who should've been given the captain's armband following stand-in skipper Dominik Szoboszlai's substitution.

In the moments immediately following the full-time whistle, Curtis Jones, who is wanted by Inter Milan, ran up to confront Szoboslai about his decision to hand the armband to Kostas Tsimikas. Tensions flared between the trio, culminating in the Greek full-back throwing the armband to the ground in dramatic fashion.

With Liverpool looking to recover from a disappointing season under Arne Slot, and in the wake of seasoned veterans Mohamed Salah and Robertson's departures, it appears the Reds may have a leadership crisis on their hands.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits Man City were 'not switched on' in dismal 3-0 Community Shield defeat and calls for transfers - while Mikel Arteta predicts huge season for Martin Odegaard after starring role
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Manchester City to be active in the transfer market before their Premier League campaign starts on Sunday — after Barcelona finally agreed a £65.4million deal to sign Rodri.

City’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield laid bare the need for central midfield reinforcements, though a move for Lille and Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is nearing completion.

Barca are finalising an agreement to land Rodri, who was not with Maresca’s squad in Cardiff.

‘Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d’Or,’ said Maresca before news of the agreement broke.

‘He’s a top player, all the teams need a player like Rodri, so it’s not about if we miss Rodri or not.’

City still hold an interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez, despite the Blues’ Friday deadline to lodge a £120m bid having passed without a formal offer being made.

Enzo Maresca has called for more transfer activity after Man City's 3-0 loss to Arsenal in the Community Shield

Man City are closing on a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi, but Barcelona are expected to make another push this week to sign £70m-rated Rodri

‘He [Bouaddi] is still a Lille player,’ Maresca said of the 18-year-old. ‘Any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week [City begin with a trip to Brighton on Sunday].

‘If they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better so they can understand the way we want to play.’

Bouaddi — who was on the bench as Lille drew at Everton in a pre-season friendly on Saturday — wants to join City and the French club’s boss Davide Ancelotti confirmed there had been negotiations between the clubs.

Tijjani Reijnders is joining Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia for £52m after just one season at the club and Maresca admitted there is business City need to do if they are to compete for the biggest trophies again this season.

Elliot Anderson, Nico O’Reilly, Jeremy Doku and Erling Haaland all started the Community Shield, despite only returning to training in midweek.

‘Elliot was quite good for his first game,’ said Maresca. ‘We decided to start with four who had just two or three sessions.

ODEGAARD STEALS THE SHOW Mikel Arteta said Arsenal can use their Community Shield thrashing of Manchester City to lay down a marker to their rivals ahead of the club's Premier League title defence. The Gunners eased past Enzo Maresca’s men after first-half goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz, before Martin Odegaard added the gloss on 48 minutes in a ruthless display. The north London club’s victory over the FA Cup holders gave them their second trophy in four months and their 18th Community Shield title overall, leaving Arteta purring. '(I'm) very impressed in the manner that we played, especially in the manner that we competed so that's a standard for us and if we have the standards at this level I'm sure that we're going to be really competitive,' warned Arteta. 'Probably there's more belief (after winning title), you know how to do it, you know what it takes to win it and the contribution of everybody because last season that was the biggest asset of the team. Every single player contributed to make us champions and we know that that's going to be exactly the same. ‘I'm obviously extremely happy with the performance, the results and winning the first trophy. We talked about the desire that we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it, and I certainly saw a lot of positive things there against a top opponent.’ Odegaard stole the show as he led from the front after an injury-plagued last season. Arteta believes a different Odegaard will be raring to prove a point this time around. He added: ‘Well, he (Odegaard) missed five or six months for different things and it was extremely difficult for him to get any momentum, so I'm sure this year if we can maintain him fit, available with the players around him, we're going to see a very different Martin. ‘And I sense from the first day that he joined that he has something else in the belly that he wants to prove and show it, because the team needs it as well.’ ISAAN KHAN

‘The reason was because sometimes players prefer to start. The plan was to change all of them after 45 minutes, or an hour maximum.’

City started sluggishly, conceding inside the first minute, and Maresca criticised his team for not being ‘switched on’.

Captain Ruben Dias said the display was ‘frustrating’. He added: ‘It’s not good enough. Many things are changing, a new manager as well. If there is a lesson to be learned in a final, let it be this one because there are a lot more coming.

‘The most important thing is we’re already looking forward and we’ll be ready for our next game.’

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy mulls surprise move to Brazil after receiving a 'considerable' offer from Sao Paulo - with West Ham also in talks with striker
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy has held talks with Brazilian side Sao Paulo.

Negotiations are in the early stages but it is understood to be a considerable offer from one of Brazil's biggest clubs who have just come out of a transfer embargo.

The 39-year-old is considering the ambitious move despite initially planning a fairytale return to the Premier League.

The former England striker has also spoken to West Ham among others.

The ex-Leicester forward wants to take his time to make the right decision for his family as they felt they rushed into their move to Cremonese last year despite valuing the experience.

Vardy had an option to stay for another season with the Lombardy outfit had they remained in Serie A.

Jamie Vardy is considering a surprise move to Brazil after receiving an early stage offer

As a free agent he can join clubs outside of the transfer window but ideally wants to decide before then.

Vardy called time on his 13-season stint at the Foxes at the end of the 2024-25 season as the club's greatest-ever player.

The former non-league star scored his 200th goal for Leicester in the dying stages of that campaign, after announcing his departure in April of last year.

The striker was instrumental to the club's golden spell in the 2010s, winning the Premier League, the FA Cup, and the Championship twice.

Sports.title: Juventus reopen talks with Tottenham's Guglielmo Vicario after Emiliano Martinez deal collapses, and Al Hilal target Chelsea's Pedro Neto: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Juve back in for Spurs' Vicario

Juventus have resumed contacts for Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario after talks for Aston Villa's Emiliano Martinez collapsed on Sunday night.

The Serie A club made an initial offer of £6million, plus performance-related bonuses for Martinez and his advisors agreed terms with Juventus intermediaries on a significant rise on his current £130,000 a week.

However, despite initial optimism, Juventus have pulled back from the deal and are back in talks for 29-year-old Vicario.

Villa have agreed a £30m deal with Parma for goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who will sign a five-year contract. The Japan international is expected to become their new number one so a solution will be required for Martinez.

Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario is again the subject of interest from Juventus after the club's move for Emiliano Martinez collapsedc

Bolton's McAtee targeted by four clubs

Bolton Wanderers forward John McAtee is attracting interest from a number of Championship clubs, with Charlton Athletic, Cardiff City, Lincoln City as well as Sheffield Wednesday all understood to have made enquiries regarding the 27-year-old.

McAtee produced an impressive performance on the club's return to the Championship on Saturday, registering two assists as Bolton secured a memorable 2-1 victory over Preston North End in their first game back in the second tier for seven years.

The Salford born forward, who turned 27 last month, has built a reputation as a versatile and hard-working attacking player capable of operating across the front line. He joined Bolton in 2024 and has made a significant contribution since arriving at the club.

His performance against Preston is likely to further increase interest, with a number of clubs now monitoring his situation as the transfer window enters its final few weeks.

McAtee, who turned 27 last month, has built a reputation as a versatile and hard-working attacking player capable of operating across the front line

Stoke's Seko heads home

Japanese midfielder Tatsuki Seko has left Stoke City to join J1 League side Urawa Reds for an undisclosed fee.

The 28-year-old returns to Japan after two seasons in the Championship with the Potters, having arrived from Kawasaki Frontale in the summer of 2024.

Newcastle keep Bergvall in their sights

Lucas Bergvall is one of the names that remains on Newcastle United's radar in the final days of the window.

While talks have taken place for Bayern Munich’s Joao Palhinha, other midfielders are being considered.

Newcastle discussed Bergvall as part of conversations over the sale of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Newcastle made further enquiries after Tonali’s sale but were told the fee would be over £50m for Bergvall.

Nottingham Forest are also expected to make another offer for the Swede.

Newcastle discussed Bergvall as part of conversations over the sale of Tonali to Tottenham and made further enquiries after but were told the fee would be over £50m

Hammers turn attention to Piroe

West Ham have enquired after Leeds United striker Joel Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for Troy Parrott at AZ Alkmaar.

The Hammers had an opening bid around £15m rejected for Parrott last week and remained in talks offering slightly more. They could yet make another offer but as it stands the deal is paused and they have enquired about Piroe with Leeds prepared to sell.

Dedic due on Tyneside tomorrow

Benfica right-back Amar Dedic is due on Tyneside tomorrow to undergo a medical ahead of his move to Newcastle.

Negotiations are at the final stages with a £29.5million deal in place for the 23-year-old.

The Bosnia international is likely to go straight into the team to play Liverpool next weekend.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering.

Coventry hold talks over £21m move for striker

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last night, Coventry City are in talks with Fenebahce over a £21million deal for striker Sidiki Cherif.

As well as agreeing to sign Nottingham Forest's Taiwo Awoniyi, manager Frank Lampard wants Cherif who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January.

The 19-year-old scored three goals in 14 games for Fenerbahce.

Neto a shock target for Al Hilal

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is wanted by Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

Neto is also on the lists of Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea's asking price is understood to be prohibitive.

Pedro Neto has emerged as a target for Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal

Tigers in for Betis star Garcia

Hull City are in talks for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia.

The 20-year-old is valued around £7million by Betis. He made his debut for Spain U21s a year ago and has scored three goals in five games for his country at that level.

Hull have been looking for a winger after a proposed deal for Aston Villa's Leon Bailey stalled.

Garcia has become a key player for coach Manuel Pellegrini owing to his pace and goal contributions.

He came on as a substitute for Antony last night in their 1-0 friendly defeat at Inter Milan on Sunday. John Stones scored the only goal, coming off the bench to score on his debut.

Hull City are in talks for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia (left)

And the best of the rest...

LEEDS have agreed a deal with HAMBURG to send Sebastiaan Bornauw on loan to the German club.

FULHAM have had a £17m bid rejected for ATALANTA right-back Raoul Bellanova. The Italians are reluctant to sell the 26-year-old this summer.

TOULOUSE left-back Dayann Methalie has arrived in the UK ahead of his medical at SUNDERLAND.

The France U21 international is set to finalise his £25.7million move pending tomorrow's medical.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

SATURDAY: Aston Villa in talks with Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki

FRIDAY: Djed Spence completes £30m move to Inter Milan

THURSDAY: Chelsea waiting for Fernandez bid

WEDNESDAY: Man United target Carlos Baleba on Newcastle's radar

TUESDAY: Roy Keane's son-in-law linked with move to Portugal

MONDAY: West Ham interested in free agent Jamie Vardy

Sports.title: Young, foreign and full of adventure... new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is everything his predecessor wasn't
Sports.content:
As is so often the case with managerial changes made in the aftermath of failure, Scotland appear to have turned on their heels and gone in a completely new direction with the appointment of Sebastien Pocognoli.

After the young Belgian was tonight confirmed as the national side’s next head coach, it’s clear the Scottish FA will be getting a man who could hardly be more different to his predecessor.

While Steve Clarke was experienced and pragmatic, but also dour and, well, Scottish, Pocognoli is a thrusting 39-year-old adventurer who will become only the second overseas coach in the country’s history, the first since Berti Vogts over two decades back.

Pocognoli and Clarke do have in common a passion for protecting and caring for their players, but this appointment is something entirely new for Scottish football’s governing body, who are recognising the nationwide appetite for change after this summer’s World Cup group-stage exit.

Yes, Clarke made history by taking Scotland to the finals of three major tournaments, but the Tartan Army ran out patience with his caution on the big stage and with his loyalty to players who were nearing, if not past, their sell-by date at that level.

And so, the SFA have sought to address those concerns with an imaginative appointment — Ole Gunnar Solskjaer is also reported to have been interviewed — whose profile, front-foot philosophy and touchline emotion will shake things up at Hampden Park.

New Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli will be an emotional presence on the touchline

Pocognoli's passion has prompted comparisons with Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone

Steve Clarke's caution on the big stage grew increasingly frustrating for the Tartan Army

Of course, it helps to tap into a fashion at times like these. Pocognoli’s biggest coaching success was at Union Saint-Gilloise, who benefited from Tony Bloom and his Jamestown Analytics empire long before Hearts. Don’t be surprised if ‘data-based’ gets a mention when Ian Maxwell and Mike Mulraney get round to explaining their rationale this week.

The season before last, Pocognoli made history by leading USG to their first league title since 1935. He also inspired them to a Belgian Cup triumph during a campaign that earned him the country’s manager of the year award. The club’s first-ever Champions League experience included victories away to PSV Eindhoven and Galatasaray.

All that earned Pocognoli a move to Monaco in October, but he lasted only seven months in the job. That was despite a 10-game unbeaten sequence and a run to the knockout playoff round of the Champions League, where they were pipped 5-4 on aggregate by Paris Saint-Germain.

He is an exciting proposition. While his coaching career is still in its infancy, he has already earned himself a reputation as a forthright, demonstrative coach, fiercely protective of his team and adept at psyching them up with stirring messages and disrespectful quotes from opponents.

Born in the Belgian city of Seraing, he is of Italian descent. Often dressed entirely in black, he is sometimes compared with the Atletico Madrid manager, Diego Simeone, although Pocognoli insists that the parallel extends no further than their personalities.

In an interview earlier this year, he said: ‘I am not calm. There is a lot of fire burning inside me — the Latin blood in my veins undoubtedly has something to do with that. My grandfathers were Italian.

‘I know about the comparison with myself and Diego Simeone. Simeone is a good coach, but he is not my great role model. Atletico Madrid’s playing style doesn’t appeal to me much either. At most, we share our Latin temperament.’

While Simeone is renowned for his teams’ counter-attacking strengths, Pocognoli takes a possession-based approach that features aggressive pressing and counter-pressing. After putting in place a structure that gives him peace of mind — 3-4-1-2 is his preferred formation — he wants players to express themselves. ‘I am very self-confident,’ he says. ‘I don’t doubt easily.’

On his arrival at Monaco from USG, Pocognoli was asked to elaborate on his principles. ‘There are two aspects: the collective and the individual,’ he replied. ‘My role is to establish a structure where the defenders are dependent on the work of the attackers. This is what my team did very well last year. This resulted in one of the best defences in Europe.’

As a player, Pocognoli performed well enough at left-back to earn 13 Belgium caps, although he never made it to a World Cup finals. He was involved when the country’s golden generation emerged, but he was also party to the regional factionalism that held it back. After a 4-2 home defeat by Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2009, he had a notorious dressing-room altercation with Timmy Simons and Stijn Stijnen, who accused him of not taking the result seriously.

Pocognoli started his playing career with Genk before joining AZ Alkmaar, where he won the Dutch title. After a move to Standard Liege and then Hannover 96, he had a three-year spell in England, notable mostly for his struggles at West Bromwich Albion. Out of favour with manager Tony Pulis, he went on to loan to Brighton before returning to his homeland.

The last days of his playing career were spent with USG, where he became coach of their Under-21s. That was followed by a spell in charge of Genk’s Under-18s and an age-group job with the Belgian national side before the big break came his way.

Even USG could not have imagined that, in his debut season as a manager in his own right, he would become the youngest in Belgium’s history to win a league title. Emboldened by that early success, he is hungry for more, inspired perhaps by some of the big names he has learned from.

Former Belgium team-mate Vincent Kompany is one of his role models. As is Louis van Gaal, the ‘most complete’ manager he has worked with. Pocognoli appreciated the Dutchman’s honesty when he played for him at AZ Alkmaar. ‘He taught me the most, tactically and technically. He had a very direct way of communicating, which shocked me a little at first.’

How Pocognoli, nicknamed ‘Poco’, adapts to international football should be fascinating. Will his limited access to players allow him to instil in them his distinctive way of playing? How will he fare without the recruitment that was crucial to his success in Belgium?

When he was a boy, Pocognoli wasn’t so keen on football and had ambitions to be an archaeologist. ‘I’ve always been interested in travel, culture, and adventure,’ he says. ‘Humanity inspires me. That’s what I love about my job: mixing cultures, learning from others.’

His next managerial experience will be an education all right. Let’s hope the cross-cultural experiment benefits Scotland as much as it does him.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt makes history as 'track goddess' claims her FOURTH European Championships gold with Team GB mixed 4x100m relay triumph
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt makes history as 'track goddess' claims her FOURTH European Championships gold with Team GB mixed 4x100m relay triumph

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

With arms outstretched and a grin almost as wide, Amy Hunt signed off from these European Championships in the same way she began – by claiming a gold medal. Make that four in the space of a week and a slice of history.

No woman has ever won so many from a single sitting at this level, but a perfect week for Hunt was concluded by dragging Britain to victory via a tricky spot in the mixed 4x100m relay.

Added to a gold medal secured later in the evening by Georgia Hunter Bell, and team gold in the female marathon, it was stunning day for British women in Birmingham. But Hunt was the star. Hunt was the show. Hunt was the breakthrough act that offers rich promise for the second half of this Olympic cycle.

That much was shown again on closing night, in a new relay format that has the ring of a gimmick but leant itself to an unexpectedly tight race.

It started inauspiciously when Jeremiah Azu, the men’s silver medallist, left Dina Asher-Smith in fourth at the first change, before the former 200m world champion launched her team back into the lead with a superb leg of 10.04sec. But even then, there was work to do because Zharnel Hughes, surprisingly selected ahead of Romell Glave, lost the lead to Germany.

Enter Hunt. Taking the baton for the anchor leg, she was 0.03sec behind Gina Luckenkemper, but demolished that deficit in a handful of those long strides before seeing off the closing portion in just 9.86sec. Clocking 39.97sec, 0.14sec clear of Germany, Britain had another gold and so did Hunt.

Amy Hunt helped Team GB claim gold in the mixed 100m relay on Sunday evening

The self-styled 'track goddess' aimed for a historic four medals and won them without skipping a beat

‘Oh my gosh, I am over the moon,’ said Hunt, 24. ‘To finish it off with some of my best friends in the sport is incredible.

‘Me and Jeremiah have the same birthday, so we're kind of twins. To do it all together is incredible.’

Indicating that there had been a late change of plans to the line-up, Hunt also disclosed she had only practised handovers with Hughes an hour before the gun. Clearly they had the raw speed to cope.

While Hunt’s haul is unprecedented, it will be noted that the mixed relay was only introduced this year. But that will not be counted against a Cambridge graduate who destroyed all-comers as an individual in the 100m and 200m and has added two relay titles in the course of a single weekend. She once described herself as a ‘track goddess and academic badass’ and the counter-arguments are getting harder to stage.

The forthcoming intrigue will centre on how she competes at the World Championships next year, where the best of the United States and Caribbean might offer better perspective of her level. As for Asher-Smith, 30, this was the eighth European gold medal of her career and 10th of any shade, giving her the outright female record in the 92 years of the championship.

Less than an hour later, Hunter Bell secured gold of her own in the 1500m, with a victory that was easier to predict than any of the past week. With the exception of France’s Agathe Guillemot, no one in this field had ticked off the distance within three seconds of her best mark for 2026.

But it is one thing to stand apart on paper and another to dance through the tactical minefield of a race at the sport’s most complex distance. Hunter Bell’s approach was delightfully straightforward – she set a slow pace from the front and then kicked them all the smithereens in the final 300m when Klaudia Kazimierska attempted a challenge on the last lap. Crossing in 4:07.78, Hunt Bell was well over a second clear of the Pole in silver.

Hunt praised some of her 'best friends' in the sport - team-mates Zharnel Hughes, Jeremiah Azu, and Dina Asher-Smith

Georgia Hunter Bell blew away her competition with another faultless 1500m performance

For those who follow track and field, Hunter Bell’s story is well known by now, but fresh audiences ought to watch in awe of a woman who quit for five years in her twenties and only turned professional after Olympic bronze in 2024. Prior to that decision, she was working in cyber security; in the two years since, she has now seven international medals, including golds this season at the world indoors, Commonwealth Games and here. Remarkable.

The tone for British women was set earlier in the day, when Abbie Donnelly took bronze in the marathon – the first British female to ever step on that particular podium. Coupled with the elevated placings of Natasha Wilson (fifth) and Rose Harvey (14th), Donnelly led Britain to the team gold.

Jazmin Sawyers, competing two years after rupturing an Achilles tendon, took an impressive silver in a high-level long jump showdown. Her season best mark 6.99m was only bettered by Italy’s Larissa Iapichino.

Both the men’s and women’s 4x400m teams took silver, carrying Britain to 19 medals for the Championship, but the latter’s narrow loss to Italy gave the Italians top spot in the final table.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet was exceptional in Liverpool's 2-0 win over Como, writes LEWIS STEELE - he has eased defensive concerns but next week is huge in pursuit of PSG pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye
Sports.content:
Crisis? What crisis?

Two weeks ago, it was probably fair to say Liverpool had a crisis in their defensive department and risked going into the new season incredibly undercooked.

Virgil van Dijk had not yet returned from an extended break. Joe Gomez had joined Jeremy Jacquet, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley in the injury room. Youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who was outstanding on the American tour, did not have a work permit to play official games.

A fortnight on, though, all seems well. Jacquet made his unofficial debut in a friendly against Italian overachievers Como at Anfield on Sunday and did not put a foot wrong on his first match since February 7 for former club Rennes.

Not just that – and we will return to the eye-catching Jacquet in due course – Liverpool have eased their defensive woes by signing Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan this week. The versatile Uruguay international also featured against Como.

Van Dijk is back and remains the most reliable member of the squad in terms of availability, while young Italian Leoni is beginning the final stages of his rehabilitation from a lengthy knee injury and hopes to be back by the end of September.

Jeremy Jacquet did not put a foot wrong on his unofficial debut for Liverpool in their friendly win over Como

The £60m signing's performance makes him a contender to partner Virgil van Dijk on the opening day of the season

So just like that, Iraola’s biggest pre-season worry – over who would start the campaign at centre-back – is gone.

Jacquet, who moved to Liverpool from Rennes this summer after the clubs struck a £60million agreement in January, looks a real contender to partner Van Dijk when the Reds travel to Newcastle for their league opener.

On his first touch just seconds into this friendly, the 21-year-old confidently stepped past a couple of prying attackers. Calm and composed, just what Iraola demands of his defenders who must take risks in possession.

In his last touch before a planned substitution saw him replaced by Araujo, Jacquet scored to put Liverpool 2-0 up against Cesc Fabregas’s outfit, who will compete in the Champions League this term. Easier to miss but in the right place at the right time.

It is early days and we will not overreact to Jacquet’s fine performance. Given his tender age and lack of experience at this level, he will need time to settle in a new league, especially after missing half of last season with a shoulder problem.

But the first signs are extremely encouraging. Liverpool believe he and Leoni, the 19-year-old 6ft 5in physical specimen, are two of the brightest defenders in the game.

It fills fans with more confidence that a world without Van Dijk – maybe after this season – is not so bleak.

Barcola eclipse as new winger(s) needed

Now the worries at central defence have been duly allayed, attention turns to other problem positions such as the wide forwards.

Cody Gakpo scored Liverpool’s opener and assisted Jacquet’s goal but the left winger has been widely linked with a move to Tottenham.

The club say they have no plans of selling the Dutchman but that stance might be tested if they sign Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, who is the top target.

Transfer chiefs have been in talks with PSG over a move for Barcola who, alongside fellow target Ibrahim Mbaye, was not even on the substitutes’ bench for the French and European champions in their friendly on Sunday night.

It will be a big week in that regard, with the clock ticking on Liverpool finally replacing Mohamed Salah.

Transfer chiefs have been in talks over a move for Bradley Barcola, pictured, and Ibrahim Mbaye, who were not on the bench for PSG's Super Cup clash on Sunday night

Alexander Isak is looking incredibly sharp in pre-season after a nightmare debut campaign

New signing Victor Munoz, who arrived from Osasuna this summer, looked the part and was the standout in a 0-0 draw in a training match at the AXA Training Centre earlier on Sunday before the official friendly at Anfield.

The Spaniard, who was part of the World Cup winners’ squad in the US despite not playing, also had a cameo in the later game and looks a handful. He is in a battle with Gakpo, teenager Rio Ngumoha to start against Newcastle next week.

We should also give a word to Lewis Koumas. The forward spent last year on loan at Hull City and was on the bench as the Tigers won the play-off final but has seriously caught Iraola’s eye this pre-season and could be given a chance – though clubs are circling for his signature.

Isak like a new signing

It is a cliche but Alexander Isak will be like a new signing for Liverpool.

The Swede only managed four goals and 22 appearances in a nightmare first season after his £125m controversial move from Newcastle. He looked out of shape when he arrived and then broke his fibula in December which all but ruined his campaign.

But Isak is looking incredibly sharp in pre-season after a positive World Cup under Graham Potter. He managed 83 minutes before being replaced by young striker Will Wright.

Isak could have opened the scoring early doors in this friendly but rattled the post. Nevertheless, he is looking fitter than he ever did during his first season.

With Salah’s goals no longer able to be relied upon, Isak may define whether this year is a success or not for Liverpool. There will be no better place to start than with a goal and win against his old employers Newcastle next week.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner makes stance clear on Morgan Gibbs-White's future, the wing-backs set to thrive in boss' new system... and there's still no shirt sponsor: Nottingham Forest 2-0 Brest
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner makes stance clear on Morgan Gibbs-White's future, the wing-backs set to thrive in boss' new system... and there's still no shirt sponsor: Nottingham Forest 2-0 Brest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ahead of Nottingham Forest's Premier League opener against Leeds next Saturday, Oliver Glasner has shown his hand simply by disguising it.

The 2-0 friendly victory over French club Brest, achieved thanks to first-half strikes from Chris Wood (from the penalty spot) and Luca Netz, featured few of Forest's key men.

Most of those players, including star attacker Morgan Gibbs-White, were involved in a training ground friendly against Coventry on Saturday, which Forest won 2-0.

So all things being equal, we can start to build an idea of Glasner's starting XI. In a 3-4-2-1 formation that would mean: Sels; Milenkovic, Murillo, Diomande; Aina, Schlager, Sangare, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Igor Jesus.

Glasner still wants another forward and may seek to add a right wing-back, too, but he is also keen to move on unwanted players. Daily Mail Sport examines how Forest are looking with a week to go.

Oliver Glasner disguised his hand for the opening day of the season with many of his stars featuring in a behind closed doors game on Saturday, rather than their match with Brest

What about Gibbs-White?

After selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City earlier in the summer, Glasner is adamant no more key players will leave. Nothing is certain until September 3, of course, but this was a very strong summary of the situation.

Gibbs-White changed his agent earlier this summer, which is often the prelude to a transfer. But the 26-year-old is the highest-paid player in Forest's history and would not come cheap.

Asked about Gibbs-White's future, the Forest boss said: 'It was clear after selling Elliot Anderson that none of our starters will leave the club. That's a commitment from the ownership and no player has asked to leave the club.

'[Gibbs-White leaving] was never a topic. We didn't have to talk about it – it was a non-verbal agreement. We looked each other in the eye, because we want to be successful. If we want to strengthen the squad it makes no sense to sell starters.'

Nevertheless, Glasner will still be relieved when the window closes. Gibbs-White wants to play Champions League football in the coming seasons and earlier this summer, Chelsea were showing an interest.

The Blues will not compete in Europe this term but if Enzo Fernandez were to move to Manchester City, it would be interesting to see whether they had another dart at Gibbs-White. Whether Forest would sell, though, is another matter entirely. Based on Glasner's words, Gibbs-White looks likelier to stay than depart.

Morgan Gibbs-White looks likely to stay than depart, with Glasner stressing none of their starters will leave the club

Wing-backs to have a huge role

Glasner is still trying to impose his ideas on this squad but from the Brest game, it was clear that the wing-backs will have a huge role in how Forest attack.

Eric da Silva Moreira and Luca Netz were constantly available for passes in the Brest half, with Netz having a particular impact. He won the penalty that Wood converted, and soon afterwards started and finished a fine move also involving Callum Hudson-Odoi and Nico Dominguez.

Operating as one of two No10s, Hudson-Odoi drifted wide to allow Netz to make an underlapping run inside him, and it is easy to imagine Neco Williams – the first choice in that left wing-back role – thriving in such a system.

On the other side, the future is less clear. Ola Aina is the starter as things stand yet Glasner continues to look for another player for that role, perhaps one who is a little more dynamic and more durable than the Nigerian, who has had an outstanding three years at Forest.

Luca Netz, who scored Forest's second in the 2-0 victory, could be among the wing backs to have a key role in Glasner's side

Expect more sales

Questioned about his options in central midfield, Glasner insisted he was happy with who he has and instead highlighted Forest's bloated squad.

He believes he has too many players and would like to move some on before the window closes. This was the perfect chance to put them in the shop window, which is perhaps why he played his second-string today rather than the first-choice players.

It would be no surprise to see Dilane Bakwa, Arnaud Kalimuendo, Eric da Silva Moreira or Morato go elsewhere, while Zach Abbott may be loaned to the EFL. 'It makes no sense to go into the season with 26 outfield players, especially when we do not have European football,' said Glasner.

The Austrian also revealed Forest are likely to be without club skipper Ryan Yates against Leeds next weekend due to 'a minor issue'.

Departures are expected with Glasner highlighting the bloated nature of Forest's squad

What is Chris Wood's future?

Wood made his mark from the spot after recovering from a thigh injury but it is unclear how regularly he will play.

Igor Jesus looks like Glasner's preferred No9 at this stage and although the Brazilian can play as one of the two No10s, he looks the favourite to line up against Leeds. Glasner is also looking for another striker, with Forest holding a long-term interest in Chelsea's Liam Delap.

So where does Wood fit in? Wood turns 35 in December and has a year left on his contract. With Taiwo Awoniyi poised to join Coventry, Forest do not want to leave themselves too light in attack but will Wood be willing to accept a bit-part role?

'We have two or three additions in the pipeline, let's say it like this,' said Glasner. 'It's always about the two clubs, the player and the agent. As soon as these four parties find an agreement we will have another player.

'I'm very pleased so far. We brought two top players in with Xaver Schlager and Ousmane Diomande. I think everybody can see which impact Schlager can have in our game.

'Diomande is just at the beginning of the pre-season, after a longer break after the World Cup, so he will need a little bit of time to be fully fit.

'Having two players from top leagues, who have both played more than 100 games, played for their country and played Champions League football… that will give us quality and experience. So far everything we wanted to do we already did.'

Chris Wood scored from the spot against Brest but it unclear as to the role he will play

Where is the sponsor?

Forest still do not have a front-of-shirt agreement to replace Bally's, the bookmaker who agreed an £8m deal with the club for the 2025-26 campaign.

Now Premier League clubs are forbidden from advertising betting companies on the front of their shirts which means Forest are currently without a main shirt sponsor, a week away from the new season.

Supporters may like the cleaner look, but those in the boardroom will want a new partner on board as soon as possible.

Sports.title: Luis Enrique gives frosty three-word reply as both Liverpool targets axed from PSG squad
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique gives frosty three-word reply as both Liverpool targets axed from PSG squad

Luis Enrique left both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye out of his squad for Paris Saint-Germain's clash with Lens on Sunday amid strong interest from Liverpool

View 2 Images Luis Enrique shrugged off the question post-match (Image: Ligue 1)

Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique wasn't in the mood to discuss the futures of Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye after leaving the pair out of his squad to face Lens on Sunday. PSG missed the chance to win a second trophy in five days, as they were beaten 1-0 by Lens in the Trophee des Champions.

‌



Barcola, who's valued at an eye-watering £145million, and Mbaye, valued at around £40m, watched from the stands at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis amid strong interest from Liverpool. The Reds are keen to sign both wingers in separate deals.

‌



PSG have this week brought in Ferran Torres and Mika Godts to strengthen their forward line, pushing Barcola and Mbaye down the pecking order. But even with their two new signings not ready to face Lens, Barcola and Mbaye weren't invovled either.

‌



In his post-match press conference, Enrique was asked about the decision and gave a short shrift. "Thank you, goodbye," the PSG manager replied before walking out of the media room.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Enrique wasn't best pleased after watching his side toil against Lens, who won the Coupe de France last season to set up a clash with Ligue 1 title winners PSG. Florian Thauvin scored just after the half-hour mark before Lens were reduced to 10 men before the break.

Kyllian Antonio saw red after a late studs-up challenge on Maghnes Akliouche, another forward who PSG recently signed. The hosts were forced to play with 10 men from the 39th minute onwards but held firm until the teams were balanced out.

PSG had a man sent off in the closing stages, as Nuno Mendes was given his marching orders for an elbow on Michal Skoras. Lens managed to see out the win and shocked the Champions League holders.

‌



Should Liverpool sign both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye are targets for Liverpool (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Barcola and Mbaye's futures will now be in the spotlight as the transfer window enters its final two weeks. On Saturday, Enrique made a point that if a player isn't happy at the Parc des Princes, a 'solution' needs to be found.

‌



"We are a very young, very ambitious team," the Spaniard affirmed. "It is important for us to make changes and look for players who enjoy playing our way and who love playing for PSG. That is very clear to us.

"When a player doesn't want to come here, or doesn't have a smile on their face about being here, it is better to find another solution."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Barcelona agree Rodri deal, Liverpool's Barcola boost, £60m for Arsenal to sign star
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Sunday, August 16.

Liverpool have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as a result of Paris Saint-Germain signing Mika Godts from Ajax. There was speculation that the Ligue 1 champions would be willing to trim their £145million valuation of the 23-year-old, but only if they secured a solid replacement on the left.

Having done so, it's now a waiting game to see whether the rumour mill has churned truth with regards to a potential cut-price deal for Barcola. The Frenchman has been a priority target for Liverpool for the majority of the summer, as Andoni Iraola looks for further firepower up the top end of the pitch to challenge in 2026/27.

Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to fork out at least £60m if they hope to sign Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen before next month's transfer deadline, according to sources speaking with Football Insider.

The Gunners are also looking for attacking threat this summer, having missed out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior following a long and drawn out transfer saga. They could now turn their attention to 27-year-old Osimhen, who has been linked with a move to the Premier League for the past couple of years, only for a deal to fail to come to fruition.

On the other side of North London, Tottenham Hotspur are eyeing moves for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo and Manchester City's Savinho, as a summer of massive spending continues. Reports from the Netherlands suggest that Gakpo has reached an agreement in principle with regards to personal terms, with a £70m price tag being touted for his transfer.

Savinho, meanwhile, has reportedly shared an interest in working under Roberto De Zerbi this season, with Spurs looking to wrap up an £85m move for the Brazilian.

At the Etihad Stadium, the Cityzens are on the brink of securing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in an £85m swoop of their own, as Rodri closes in on a move to Barcelona after the clubs finally agreed terms. Having already welcomed Elliot Anderson in a £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, City have now turned their attention to finding a suitable playing partner for the 23-year-old.

Bouaddi, 18, could be just that, following a formidable World Cup campaign with Morocco.

Stay tuned for all of the latest news and updates in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet scores on Liverpool debut as Cody Gakpo sends reminder - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet scores on Liverpool debut as Cody Gakpo sends reminder - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-0 COMO: Goals from Cody Gakpo and Jeremy Jacquet ended pre-season on a high for the Reds, with Andoni Iraola getting another look at his squad at Anfield

View 5 Images Liverpool paid £60million to sign Jeremy Jacquet (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Liverpool rounded out pre-season with a comfortable 2-0 win against Cesc Fabregas' Como. New signing Jeremy Jacquet was among the goals, while Cody Gakpo opened the scoring amid uncertainty over his future.

‌



Andoni Iraola's side head to Newcastle next Sunday, so it was a final chance for the new Reds boss to get a look at his players in action. Ronald Araujo also made his first appearance for Liverpool since joining on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

‌



A quirk of this fixture was that the two teams had already played each other in a behind-closed-doors game earlier in the day. It finished 0-0 at Liverpool's AXA Training Centre, with Alexis Mac Allister the notable inclusion.

‌



Here are five talking points from Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



1. Jones absent again amid Inter interest

When team news was released, all eyes were on whether Curtis Jones would make his return to the Liverpool squad. But the midfielder was missing for the second game running, with his future on Merseyside uncertain.

Italian giants Inter Milan are preparing a new bid for Jones, who's reportedly keen on the move to San Siro. Liverpool say that the 25-year-old has been dealing with a hip problem and trained alone on Sunday.

Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Inter Milan want to sign the injured Curtis Jones (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

2. Gakpo sends timely reminder

Another player who's been linked with an exit is Gakpo. Tottenham are understood to be pushing to sign the Netherlands international, with reports claiming that personal terms have already been agreed.

But Gakpo has remained professional and finished off a flowing move to break the deadlock on 23 minutes. Jeremie Frimpong drove inside from right-back and lifted the ball over Como's defence.

‌



Gakpo controlled it well and slotted home in one motion, sending a reminder to the Reds of what they'd be losing if they sell him to Tottenham. With Mo Salah gone, can Liverpool afford to lose another established forward?

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo is a target for Tottenham (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

3. Jacquet's good first impression

With half-time looming, Como looked the more likely to score after a decent spell. But it was Liverpool who ended up doubling their lead before the interval.

‌



Jacquet - making his first appearance of pre-season after recovering from a knee injury - was the scorer, given a simple tap-in from Gakpo's low cross. It was a gift for the centre-back, who's had to be patient to get his chance.

There was more to Jacquet's performance than his goal, though. The former Rennes prospect was enjoying himself defensively; showing composure on the ball, putting in challenges and made a goal-saving tackle shortly before his strike.

Jacquet was replaced at half-time, as Araujo made his Anfield bow. Lewis Koumas - who'd played 25 minutes in the earlier game - was also introduced, coming on for Rio Ngumoha.

‌



View 5 Images Jeremy Jacquet scored a goal - and prevented one (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

4. The Wirtz conundrum

When Liverpool shelled out a then-club-record £116million to sign Florian Wirtz a year ago, it was expected that he'd be rocking and rolling by now. But something still hasn't clicked.

The ex-Bayer Leverkusen star showed plenty of neat touches but didn't cause Como enough problems with his passing or dribbling. Fans are starting to doubt whether Wirtz deserves a starting berth, especially with Mac Allister on the verge of a return.

‌



Given time, one would expect his partnership with Alexander Isak to bear fruit. For now, though, perhaps pushing Dominik Szoboszlai further forward is a right call.

View 5 Images Florian Wirtz is a concern for Andoni Iraola (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

5. Next stop: St James' Park

So that's that. Liverpool's 2026 pre-season campaign is complete. The Reds have come away with three wins, two defeats and one draw from their six friendlies.

‌



Now the focus is on facing Newcastle, who've had a summer of change of their own. Iraola has a few selection headaches before next Sunday's visit to Tyneside, but could he have Bradley Barcola at his disposal?

Liverpool's top target remains at Paris Saint-Germain player and is valued at £145m. But with the transfer window closing in just over two weeks, PSG could be tempted to budge.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'

Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard inspired his team to a fine 3-0 win over Manchester City to clinch the Community Shield - and then immediately set his sights on more silverware

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard insists Arsenal are coming for more silverware this season (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Martin Odegaard helped Arsenal humiliate Manchester City - before warning his rivals Mikel Arteta's men are on a mission to win everything this season.

‌



Arsenal swept City aside 3-0 to win the Community Shield in Cardiff, thanks to goals from Riccardo Califiori, Kai Havertz and Odegaard - his first in 2026. And Odegaard told the rest of the Premier League how champions Arsenal have the hunger for as many trophies as possible.

‌



Odegaard said: "We played some brilliant football. We showed our level. We showed we're ready, serious and want to do it again.

‌



"We want to attack it. When you get a taste of how nice it is, you want to do it again. We want to win everything."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arteta has now won two trophies in the last four months and he said: "I'm extremely happy with the performance. We talked about the desire we have - and to show how much we want it.

‌



"It's down to the preparation. I'm very impressed in the manner we played and competed.

"There is more belief. How to do it (win the title), and what it means. It makes a difference. I want to live those moments again. But we know it's going to demand something special."

This was Enzo Maresca's worst possible start to his mission of replacing Pep Guardiola. It was also his joint heaviest defeat as a manager in England.

‌



View 2 Images Odegaard and Kai Havertz celebrate Arsenal's killer third goal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

He said: "The big part of the game was the first goal we conceded. Then the second one made it more difficult.

"I'm always concerned, even when we win games. We have a lot of things we need to do better.

‌



"We will re-set, analyse the game and start thinking about the next one. We can find many things after this kind of defeat. We were not switched on."

Captain Ruben Dias insisted there was a lot of work for his side to do. He said: "It's obviously not good enough. It is a final that we all wanted to win.

"If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one. You need to push through and make things work between us.

Article continues below

"We need to keep on working. and there's going to be lots of challenges along the way."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'

Cristiano Ronaldo has entered the last year of his contract with Al-Nassr after playing his final World Cup with Portugal, and the 41-year-old has opened up on his future plans

View 2 Images Retirement is near for Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has dropped a bombshell and revealed that this season will 'probably' his last. Ronaldo, 41, only has one year left on his mega-money contract with Al-Nassr, having previously admitted that he's in the final knockings of his prestigious career.

‌



The Portugal captain played at his sixth and final World Cup over the summer, as his nation crashed out in the quarter-finals with a 1-0 loss against eventual champions Spain. Speaking for the first time since Portugal's heartbreak in an interview with Vogue Magazine, Ronaldo has suggested that this season will be his last.

‌



"This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy," he stated. "I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.

‌



"Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned. Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

The interview took place five days before Ronaldo married his long-term partner, Georgina Rodriguez, in an intimate ceremony at their home in Cascais, Portugal. Earlier this week, the former Manchester United megastar returned to Saudi Arabia but didn't feature in Al-Nassr's opening game of the season.

The Saudi champions began their title defence with a 3-0 victory over Al-Fateh under new manager Ange Postecoglou. Their former boss, Jorge Jesus, left at the end of last season and is now Portugal's head coach.

Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Jesus said that the door was open for Ronaldo to receive a call-up, with their next match scheduled for late September. "I haven't spoken to Cris yet. He will never be a problem for the national team or for me," Jesus explained.

‌



Should Cristiano Ronaldo retire next year? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo couldn't achieve his World Cup dream (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

"As for the controversy, everyone is entitled to their own opinion. When the time comes to make a decision, I will speak with Cris and with everyone else individually. Cris is a symbol of Portugal. He will go down in history.

Article continues below

"It has been a great pleasure working with him. He is incredibly easy to work with. I need to speak with him to find out what he wants to do. He has always told me that he wants to finish his career at Al-Nassr. If he is in a position to be called up, I will do so."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been tipped to leave Arsenal before the summer transfer window closes, with both Manchester United and Chelsea reportedly being offered the chance to sign him

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly didn't take long to impress (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has once again questioned Arsenal's stance on selling Myles Lewis-Skelly after the Gunners star provided a gorgeous assist inside the first minute against Manchester City. Lewis-Skelly, 19, set up Riccardo Calafiori to give Arsenal an early lead in Sunday's Community Shield clash in Cardiff.

‌



The midfielder expertly turned on the ball to get away from Phil Foden before sending slide-rule pass through to Calafiori, who finished with aplomb past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was reminder to Mikel Arteta of just what Lewis-Skelly can do - even against top opposition.

‌



Reacting to the opener, Carragher posted on X: "MLS role in that arsenal goal! Are Arsenal really looking to push him out," along with two emojis.

‌



Lewis-Skelly - who's under contract until 2030 - started the game in midfield, the position in which he finished last season after largely playing at left-back since making his breakthrough. But Lewis-Skelly's future was plunged into doubt last week after both Manchester United and Chelsea were offered the chance to sign him, with Arsenal having bought Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking earlier this week, Carragher described the uncertainty surrounding Lewis-Skelly's future as 'strange', surmising that Arsenal want to offload him rather the player himself wanting to leave. "That's the thing that was a little bit strange about it," the Liverpool legend said on The Overlap Fan Debate.

"It felt almost like Arsenal offered Manchester United Myles Lewis-Skelly. It wasn't Myles Lewis-Skelly saying, I want to leave, or his people putting something out. That's where the shock came from, not so much the players' side of it."

"I still can't believe it. Obviously, last season wasn't great for him for the whole season, but when a young player has already put in performances like I've seen him put in at the Bernabeu (against Real Madrid) - maybe over a year or 18 months ago, at left-back, he was running the game at the Bernabeu – and then his performance in the final in central midfield against Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



"You can't play at that level unless you're pretty special at that age. All young players have ups and downs. Last season he didn't play as much as he probably would have liked.

Should Arsenal sell Myles Lewis-Skelly? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher doesn't understand why Arsenal would sell Myles Lewis-Skelly (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



"But his ceiling is so high for the performances he's already put in as a 20-year-old kid. I couldn't believe that Arsenal would even think about letting him go. It does feel like a strange one."

Arsenal boss Arteta was asked about Lewis-Skelly on Wednesday, with the 19-year-old having scored in a pre-season friendly. "I'm not going to talk about speculation," Arteta replied.

"If there is speculation about our players, it's a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job."

Article continues below

The Gunners manager went on to say: "He's had a really good pre-season. We asked him to play in a different position because he played more as a No.6 - we obviously lacked midfielders from international duty - and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Sports.title: Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing
Sports.content:
Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing

Norwich City winger Matej Jurasek joined Sparta Prague on a season-long loan earlier this week, but endured a hostile reception from his new club's fans

View 2 Images Sparta Prague's players and supporters clashed over the signing of Matej Jurasek on Saturday night

Sparta Prague coach Brian Priske was forced to step in after Matej Jurasek endured a hostile reception from fans of his new club. Jurasek joined Sparta on a season-long loan from Norwich City earlier this week and made his debut against FK Teplice off the bench on Saturday.

‌



But supporters of Sparta have clearly not forgotten Jurasek’s past with rivals Slavia Prague. Their anger reportedly stems in part from footage from the winger’s time at Slavia in which he appeared in a balaclava while joining anti-Sparta chants.

‌



Even though he was only on the pitch for the final 15 minutes, his every touch was booed, and he was the subject of chants that said 'we don't want you here'. His side’s post-match lap of appreciation was cut short amid the abuse directed towards the winger.

‌



Jurasek did engage in conversation with that section of supporters, telling them: "I'm a young player and I came here to win. I apologise for the statements I made against your club."

Then, after the game, Sparta coach Priske, along with a number of his players, approached his side’s supporters to defend Jurasek. Speaking to Oneplay Sport afterwards, Priske said: "It is clear that the arrival of Matej has caused a lot of reactions in the Czech Republic.

“We all expected it and knew that there would be different opinions around him. These are of course always welcome, as long as they are expressed in a decent way.

‌



"He knew that coming to Sparta would mean enormous pressure and would provoke strong reactions. Nevertheless, he decided to come with one goal - to help us.

“From the conversations we had together, I know that he is well aware of the whole situation and knows that he is not in a very good position with some of the fans at the moment.

View 2 Images Matej Jurasek in action for Norwich City against Stoke City last season (Image: (David Watts/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

‌



"It gave Matej a chance to express his feelings and apologise to many Spartans. It was a good moment to let out all the emotions that had built up over the past few days."

Jurasek featured in Norwich's first competitive game of the season, having come off the bench in their Carabao Cup first-round win against League One side MK Dons last week. And Sparta will have the option to make the Czech Republic international's move permanent at the end of the season.

"I think those 15 or 20 minutes today showed why we brought him in. Now it's up to him. He has to prove to the fans that he's one of us," Priske added.

Article continues below

"His job is to do everything he can to make sure that all those amazing Spartan fans are chanting his name next year for a completely different reason and in a positive spirit."
